chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
subject: physics

sections.title: What makes a body rigid

board_events.text: What makes a body rigid?
Until now every object was a single point: fine for where it goes, useless for how it spins.
A point has no size, so it can never rotate about itself, wobble, or roll.
Rigid body: the distance between any two particles never changes, whatever forces act.

board_events.text: Bats, flywheels, spanners deform so little that treating them as perfectly rigid predicts beautifully.
That frozen internal geometry is the one defining property of rigidity.
It is exactly what lets us treat the rotation of the whole body as one thing.

segments.text: <curious> Here is a question that quietly runs under this whole chapter: what actually makes something a rigid body?
Until this point you treated every object as a single dot carrying mass. That works perfectly when all you care about is where the thing travels.
But a dot has no size, so it can never rotate about itself, wobble, or roll. To study spinning at all, we need objects with real extent.
So hold on to this definition: a rigid body is one in which the distance between any two of its particles stays exactly the same, no matter what forces act on it.
Picture the body as a swarm of particles welded together by unbreakable, unstretchable rods. Push or twist it however you like, and the whole swarm moves and turns as one.
Real objects do deform a little, but for a cricket bat, a flywheel, a spanner, or a planet, that deformation is so tiny that treating them as perfectly rigid gives excellent predictions.
That frozen internal geometry is the single defining property of rigidity.
And it is exactly what lets us talk about the rotation of the body as one object, instead of every particle doing its own separate thing.
<curious> यहाँ एक सवाल है जो पूरे chapter के नीचे चुपचाप चलता है — आख़िर कोई चीज़ rigid body बनती कैसे है?
अब तक आप हर object को एक single point मानते आए हैं, जिसमें बस mass रखी हो। यह तब perfect है जब आपको सिर्फ़ यह देखना हो कि चीज़ जाती कहाँ है।
लेकिन point का कोई size नहीं होता, इसलिए वह न घूम सकता है, न wobble कर सकता है, न roll। Rotation पढ़ने के लिए हमें extent वाली objects चाहिए।
तो यह definition पकड़ लीजिए — rigid body वह है जिसमें किन्हीं भी दो particles के बीच की distance बिलकुल same रहती है, चाहे कोई भी force लगे।
Body को ऐसे सोचिए जैसे particles का एक swarm हो, जो unbreakable, unstretchable rods से weld किया गया हो। जैसे भी push या twist करो, पूरा swarm एक साथ मुड़ता है।
Real objects थोड़ा deform होते ज़रूर हैं, पर cricket bat, flywheel, spanner या planet के लिए वह deformation इतना छोटा है कि उन्हें perfectly rigid मानना excellent predictions देता है।
यही frozen internal geometry, rigidity की एकमात्र defining property है।
और यही हमें पूरी body के rotation की बात करने देता है, बजाय इसके कि हर particle अपना अलग खेल खेले।

board_events.text: Pure translation: every particle shares one velocity; parallel paths, no turning.
In pure translation the body behaves exactly like a single point at its centre of mass.
Pure rotation: every particle circles one fixed axis, sharing the same angular speed.
Farther from the axis means faster: $v = r\omega$.
General motion: translation and rotation at once, and a rolling wheel is the headline case.
Master strategy: split general motion into translation of the CoM plus rotation about the CoM.

segments.text: Every motion a rigid body can perform is one of just three kinds, or a blend of the first two. Get these three straight and the whole chapter feels obvious.
Look at the three panels. On the left, pure translation; in the middle, pure rotation; on the right, the two combined.

First, pure translation. Every particle moves with the very same velocity at every instant, tracing parallel paths. A book slid flat across a table is translating, and a line drawn on it keeps pointing the same way.
Because there is no turning, the whole body behaves exactly like a single particle sitting at its centre of mass. That is why everything you learned in straight-line mechanics still applies.
Second, pure rotation about a fixed axis. Every particle moves in a circle, and all those circles are centred on one fixed line, the axis. A ceiling fan and a potter wheel do exactly this.
Here every particle shares the same angular speed, but particles farther from the axis move faster. That relationship, v equals r omega, is one we will lean on again and again.
Third, general motion, where translation and rotation happen together. A rolling wheel is the headline example: its centre glides forward while the wheel spins about that centre.

<excited> And here is the master strategy of the entire chapter: split any general motion into translation of the centre of mass plus rotation about the centre of mass. Handle each with its own laws, then add the results.
कोई भी rigid body सिर्फ़ तीन तरह की motion कर सकती है — या पहले दो का blend। ये तीन clear हो गईं, तो पूरा chapter आसान लगने लगता है।
इन तीन panels को देखिए — बाईं ओर pure translation, बीच में pure rotation, और दाईं ओर दोनों का मेल।

पहली, pure translation। हर particle हर instant पर बिलकुल same velocity से चलता है, parallel paths बनाते हुए। मेज़ पर सरकती किताब translate कर रही है, और उस पर खींची line same दिशा में ही point करती रहती है।
क्योंकि कोई turning नहीं है, पूरी body अपने centre of mass पर बैठे एक single particle की तरह behave करती है। इसीलिए straight-line mechanics का सब कुछ यहाँ भी लागू होता है।
दूसरी, fixed axis के बारे में pure rotation। हर particle एक circle में घूमता है, और वे सारे circles एक fixed line — axis — पर centred होते हैं। ceiling fan और potter wheel यही करते हैं।
यहाँ हर particle का angular speed same होता है, पर axis से जितना दूर, उतना तेज़। यही relation, v बराबर r omega, आगे बार-बार काम आएगा।
तीसरी, general motion, जिसमें translation और rotation एक साथ चलते हैं। rolling wheel सबसे बड़ा example है: उसका centre आगे glide करता है जबकि wheel उसी centre के बारे में spin करता है।

<excited> और यहाँ पूरे chapter की master strategy है — किसी भी general motion को centre of mass के translation plus centre of mass के बारे में rotation में तोड़ दीजिए। हर हिस्से को उसके अपने laws से handle करो, फिर results जोड़ दो।

board_events.text: Toss a spinning bat: every part traces its own complicated, looping path.
Yet one special point traces a clean parabola: exactly a thrown-stone path.
Centre of mass = the mass-weighted average position of all the matter.
Mass-weighted: the balance point leans toward the heavier particle.
It replaces a whole system of particles with one equivalent particle of mass $M$.
The CoM moves as if all the mass, and all external force, acted at that one point.

segments.text: <curious> Toss a cricket bat spinning across the room and watch it closely. Could you predict where the handle will be in half a second? Almost nobody can.
But look at the picture. Hidden inside that tumbling bat is one special point that ignores all the chaos and quietly traces a clean, simple parabola, the very path a single thrown stone would follow.
Every other part of the bat, the handle, the toe, the edges, loops and wheels in a complicated way that looks completely random.
That one calm point is the centre of mass, and its motion is beautifully simple even while everything around it flails.
So what is it really? The centre of mass is the mass-weighted average position of all the matter in a system. That phrase, mass-weighted, is the whole idea.

If you have a light particle and a heavy one, the balance point does not sit halfway. It leans toward the heavy particle, because the heavy one pulls the average toward itself, exactly like a heavy uncle and a small child on a see-saw.

Why invent this point? Because a real object is millions of particles, each on its own path. The centre of mass lets us replace that whole messy system with one equivalent particle of total mass M, sitting at a single spot.
This gives the cleanest definition: the centre of mass moves as though the entire mass were concentrated there, and as though every external force acted there. That is the power it hands us.
<curious> एक cricket bat को घुमाते हुए कमरे में उछालिए और ध्यान से देखिए। क्या आप बता सकते हैं कि आधे second में handle कहाँ होगा? शायद ही कोई बता पाए।
पर picture देखिए। उस tumbling bat के अंदर एक ख़ास point छिपा है जो सारे chaos को नज़रअंदाज़ करके चुपचाप एक clean, simple parabola बनाता है — ठीक वही path जो एक फेंका हुआ पत्थर बनाता।
Bat का बाक़ी हर हिस्सा — handle, toe, edges — इतने complicated तरीके से loop करता है कि बिलकुल random लगता है।
वही एक शांत point है centre of mass, और उसकी motion बेहद simple रहती है, चाहे आस-पास सब कुछ उछल-कूद करे।
तो यह असल में है क्या? Centre of mass, system की सारी matter की mass-weighted average position है। वह phrase — mass-weighted — ही पूरी बात है।

अगर एक light particle हो और एक heavy, तो balance point बीच में नहीं बैठता। वह heavy particle की तरफ़ झुकता है, क्योंकि भारी वाला average को अपनी ओर खींचता है — बिलकुल see-saw पर भारी uncle और छोटे बच्चे की तरह।

यह point invent क्यों करें? क्योंकि real object लाखों particles है, हर एक अपने path पर। Centre of mass उस पूरे messy system को एक ही equivalent particle से बदल देता है, जिसकी total mass M हो और जो एक single जगह बैठा हो।
इससे सबसे साफ़ definition मिलती है — centre of mass ऐसे चलता है मानो पूरी mass वहीं concentrated हो, और मानो हर external force वहीं act कर रहा हो। यही इसकी ताक़त है।

sections.title: Two surprises and a subtle cousin

board_events.text: Two surprises, and a subtle cousin

board_events.caption: A ring centre of mass sits in empty space

board_events.text: Mass need not exist at the CoM: a ring CoM sits at its empty centre.
The CoM is a property of the body, not of your coordinate system.
Shift the origin or rotate the axes: the balance point stays welded to the object.
Centre of gravity coincides with the CoM only when $g$ is uniform over the body.
For a kilometre-tall tower, $g$ varies with height and the CG drifts just below the CoM.
Internal forces, however violent, can never move the CoM on their own.

segments.text: Two facts about the centre of mass surprise almost every student, and a subtle cousin trips them up in exams. Let us clear all three now.
First look at the ring. Its balance point sits right at the geometric centre, in the empty air, where there is literally no metal at all.
So the first surprise: mass need not exist at the centre of mass. A hollow box is the same, its centre of mass floats in the empty space inside.
Second, the centre of mass is a property of the body itself, not of the coordinate system you draw around it.
Shift your origin, rotate your axes however you like, and the physical balance point stays welded to the very same spot on the object. The numbers change; the point does not.
Now the subtle cousin, the centre of gravity. It coincides with the centre of mass only when gravity is the same at every point of the body. For everyday objects on Earth this is essentially perfect.
But for something enormous, a mountain or a tower a kilometre tall, gravity weakens slightly with height, and the centre of gravity drifts a tiny bit below the centre of mass.
<whisper> And keep one exam secret in your pocket: internal forces, however violent, can never move the centre of mass by themselves. Only external forces can.
Centre of mass के बारे में दो बातें लगभग हर student को चौंकाती हैं, और एक subtle cousin exam में फँसाता है। तीनों अभी साफ़ कर लेते हैं।
पहले ring देखिए। उसका balance point ठीक geometric centre पर बैठता है — उस खाली हवा में, जहाँ सचमुच कोई metal ही नहीं है।
तो पहली surprise — mass का centre of mass पर होना ज़रूरी नहीं। Hollow box भी वैसा ही है, उसका centre of mass अंदर की खाली जगह में तैरता है।
दूसरी, centre of mass खुद body की property है, उस coordinate system की नहीं जो आप उसके चारों ओर खींचते हैं।
Origin shift कर दो, axes जैसे चाहे rotate कर दो — physical balance point object की उसी जगह से जुड़ा रहता है। Numbers बदलते हैं, point नहीं।
अब वह subtle cousin — centre of gravity। यह centre of mass से तभी coincide करता है जब gravity body के हर point पर same हो। धरती पर रोज़मर्रा की objects के लिए यह practically perfect है।
पर किसी विशाल चीज़ के लिए — पहाड़, या एक किलोमीटर ऊँचा tower — gravity height के साथ थोड़ी कमज़ोर होती है, और centre of gravity, centre of mass से ज़रा नीचे खिसक जाता है।
<whisper> और एक exam secret जेब में रखिए — internal forces चाहे कितने भी violent हों, centre of mass को अपने आप कभी नहीं हिला सकते। सिर्फ़ external forces हिला सकते हैं।

sections.title: The centre-of-mass toolkit

board_events.text: The centre-of-mass toolkit

board_events.latex: x_{cm} = \frac{\sum m_i x_i}{M},\quad y_{cm} = \frac{\sum m_i y_i}{M},\quad z_{cm} = \frac{\sum m_i z_i}{M}

board_events.text: Origin at the CoM makes $\sum m_i \vec{r}_i = 0$.
Densities: linear $\lambda$ in kg per m, surface $\sigma$ in kg per m squared, volume $\rho$ in kg per m cubed.

segments.text: Here is the complete toolkit for the centre of mass. Every problem in this subtopic is one of these lines in disguise, so let us read each one aloud.
The master definition: the centre-of-mass position vector equals the sum of each mass times its position vector, divided by the total mass. It is a weighted average, with mass as the weight.
Break it into components and you get three identical equations. The x, the y, and the z of the centre of mass are each the mass-weighted average of that one coordinate.
For just two particles, the case you will use most for quick checks, it collapses to m one x one plus m two x two, all over m one plus m two.
When the body is continuous rather than a handful of points, the sum becomes an integral: one over M times the integral of r dee m over the whole body.

<excited> And the single most powerful line: the net external force equals total mass times the acceleration of the centre of mass. The whole system obeys Newton second law as if it were one particle.
One elegant property: if you place your origin right at the centre of mass, the mass-weighted sum of the position vectors is exactly zero.

Finally the densities you will reach for in continuous bodies. Linear lambda per metre, surface sigma per square metre, and volume rho per cubic metre, matched to whether the body is a wire, a sheet, or a solid.
यह रहा centre of mass का पूरा toolkit। इस subtopic का हर problem इन्हीं lines में से किसी एक का रूप है, तो हर एक को पढ़ लेते हैं।
Master definition — centre of mass का position vector, हर mass और उसके position vector के product के sum को total mass से भाग देने पर मिलता है। यह एक weighted average है, जिसमें weight mass है।
इसे components में तोड़िए तो तीन एक जैसे equations मिलते हैं। Centre of mass का x, y और z, हर एक उस एक coordinate का mass-weighted average है।
सिर्फ़ दो particles के लिए, जो quick checks में सबसे ज़्यादा काम आता है, यह सिमट जाता है m one x one plus m two x two, बटा m one plus m two।
जब body continuous हो, कुछ गिने-चुने points नहीं, तो sum एक integral बन जाता है — one बटा M गुणा पूरी body पर r dee m का integral।
<excited> और सबसे powerful line — net external force बराबर total mass गुणा centre of mass का acceleration। पूरा system, Newton के second law को ऐसे मानता है मानो वह एक ही particle हो।
एक elegant property — अगर origin ठीक centre of mass पर रखें, तो position vectors का mass-weighted sum बिलकुल zero हो जाता है।
आख़िर में वे densities जो continuous bodies में लगेंगी। Linear lambda per metre, surface sigma per square metre, और volume rho per cubic metre, इस हिसाब से कि body wire है, sheet है, या solid।

board_events.text: Newton third law: internal forces cancel in pairs, so $\sum \vec{F}_i^{\,int} = 0$.
Corollary: zero external force means $\vec{v}_{cm}$ is constant, so momentum is conserved.

segments.text: This is the classic derivation C B S E asks for, and it reveals exactly why the centre of mass is special. We want to prove that the total external force equals total mass times the acceleration of the centre of mass.

Keep this picture in mind the whole way: a bomb flying as one body, then exploding. The fragments scatter everywhere, yet the centre of mass keeps gliding along the original parabola. The derivation is about to explain why.

Step one, start from the definition. Multiply through by the total mass so that M times the centre-of-mass vector equals the sum of each mass times its own position vector. Clearing the fraction keeps the algebra clean.

Step two, differentiate once with respect to time. Since the masses are constant, differentiation passes straight through, giving M times the centre-of-mass velocity equals the sum of each mass times its velocity. That single line is the total momentum, and it is the bridge to momentum conservation.

Step three, differentiate again to bring in acceleration, then replace each mass-times-acceleration using Newton second law. Every particle feels two kinds of force: external ones like gravity and applied pushes, and internal ones between the particles themselves.

Step four is the heart of it. By Newton third law, for every internal push that particle A gives particle B, particle B pushes back equally and oppositely. Summed over the whole body, these pairs cancel exactly, so the internal forces add to zero.
What survives is the result: the net external force equals total mass times the acceleration of the centre of mass. The internal forces have vanished completely.

<excited> And the corollary falls out for free. If the net external force is zero, the centre-of-mass velocity is constant, so total momentum is conserved. Every recoil, collision, and explosion later in this chapter is really a centre-of-mass statement in disguise.

यह वही classic derivation है जो C B S E माँगता है, और यह ठीक-ठीक बताता है कि centre of mass ख़ास क्यों है। हमें prove करना है कि total external force बराबर total mass गुणा centre of mass का acceleration।

पूरे रास्ते यह picture याद रखिए — एक bomb एक body की तरह उड़ रहा है, फिर explode होता है। Fragments हर तरफ़ बिखरते हैं, फिर भी centre of mass उसी original parabola पर सरकता रहता है। Derivation अभी बताएगा क्यों।

Step one — definition से शुरू करो। दोनों तरफ़ total mass से गुणा कर दो, ताकि M गुणा centre-of-mass vector बराबर हो हर mass और उसके अपने position vector के product के sum के। Fraction हटाने से algebra साफ़ रहती है।

Step two — time के respect में एक बार differentiate करो। Masses constant हैं, इसलिए differentiation सीधे निकल जाती है और मिलता है M गुणा centre-of-mass velocity बराबर हर mass गुणा उसकी velocity का sum। यही एक line total momentum है, और यही momentum conservation का पुल है।

Step three — acceleration लाने के लिए फिर differentiate करो, फिर हर mass-गुणा-acceleration को Newton के second law से replace करो। हर particle पर दो तरह के force हैं — external जैसे gravity और applied pushes, और internal जो particles के आपस में हैं।

Step four ही असली दिल है। Newton के third law से, particle A जो internal push particle B को देता है, particle B वैसा ही बराबर और opposite push वापस देता है। पूरी body पर जोड़ो तो ये pairs बिलकुल cancel हो जाते हैं, इसलिए internal forces का sum zero है।
जो बचता है वही result है — net external force बराबर total mass गुणा centre of mass का acceleration। Internal forces पूरी तरह ग़ायब हो गए।

<excited> और corollary मुफ़्त में मिल जाता है। अगर net external force zero है, तो centre-of-mass velocity constant है, यानी total momentum conserved। इस chapter के आगे हर recoil, collision और explosion असल में centre of mass का ही एक छुपा हुआ बयान है।

board_events.text: Place the centre at the origin, flat side on the x-axis. By symmetry $x_{cm} = 0$.
About $0.64R$ above the centre: in empty space, no wire there.
Choose the element so every point of it shares the coordinate you are averaging.

segments.text: When symmetry does not simply hand you the answer, you integrate. Let us locate the centre of mass of a uniform semicircular wire of radius R, the most-asked version of this skill.

Set it up as in the figure: the centre at the origin, the flat diameter along the x-axis, the curve in the upper half. Take a small arc element at angle theta, subtending a tiny angle dee theta, sitting at height R sine theta.
By symmetry the left and right halves mirror each other, so the x-coordinate of the centre of mass is zero. All the work is in finding the y-coordinate.

Write the mass element. The linear density is the total mass over the arc length pi R. The element has arc length R dee theta, so its mass dee m is M over pi times dee theta, and the R cancels beautifully.

Now assemble the integral. The y of the centre of mass is one over M times the integral of the height, R sine theta, times the mass element, from theta equals zero to pi. The M cancels, leaving R over pi times the integral of sine theta.
That integral of sine, taken from zero to pi, is minus cosine evaluated across the range, which comes out to two. So the y of the centre of mass is two R over pi.

Put a number on it. Two over pi is about zero point six four, so the centre of mass sits about zero point six four R above the centre, floating in empty space where there is no wire at all. A perfect illustration that mass need not sit at the centre of mass.

<whisper> Here is the one habit that makes every continuous-body problem work: choose your element so that every point of it shares the very coordinate you are averaging. Otherwise the integral quietly lies to you.
जब symmetry सीधे answer न दे, तब integrate करते हैं। एक uniform semicircular wire, radius R, का centre of mass निकालते हैं — इस skill का सबसे ज़्यादा पूछा जाने वाला रूप।

Figure की तरह set करो — centre origin पर, flat diameter x-axis के साथ, curve ऊपर वाले आधे में। angle theta पर एक छोटा arc element लो, जो नन्हा सा dee theta बनाता है और height R sine theta पर बैठता है।
Symmetry से बायाँ और दायाँ आधा एक-दूसरे का mirror है, इसलिए centre of mass का x-coordinate zero है। सारा काम y-coordinate निकालने में है।

Mass element लिखो। Linear density है total mass बटा arc length pi R। Element की arc length R dee theta है, तो उसका mass dee m बनता है M बटा pi गुणा dee theta, और R बड़े सुंदर तरीके से cancel हो जाता है।
अब integral जमाओ। Centre of mass का y है one बटा M गुणा height R sine theta और mass element का integral, theta बराबर zero से pi तक। M cancel, बचता है R बटा pi गुणा sine theta का integral।
Sine का, zero से pi तक, integral है minus cosine, जिसे range पर evaluate करने पर two मिलता है। तो centre of mass का y है two R बटा pi।

इस पर एक number रखो। Two बटा pi लगभग zero point six four है, तो centre of mass, centre से क़रीब zero point six four R ऊपर बैठता है, खाली हवा में तैरता, जहाँ wire है ही नहीं। यह perfect मिसाल है कि mass का centre of mass पर होना ज़रूरी नहीं।
<whisper> यह रही वह एक आदत जो हर continuous-body problem को चलाती है — element ऐसे चुनो कि उसका हर point वही coordinate share करे जिसका आप average निकाल रहे हो। वरना integral चुपचाप झूठ बोल देता है।

board_events.text: Given: 2 kg at $(0,0)$, 3 kg at $(4,0)$, 5 kg at $(0,3)$; total $M = 10$ kg.

board_events.latex: x_{cm} = \frac{\sum m_i x_i}{M},\qquad y_{cm} = \frac{\sum m_i y_i}{M}

board_events.text: Centre of mass at $(1.2\ \text{m},\ 1.5\ \text{m})$.
Sanity check: the point leans toward the heavier 5 kg mass on the y-axis.

segments.text: A clean board-level example to lock in the formula. Three point masses of two, three, and five kilograms sit at three corners, and we want the coordinates of their centre of mass.

The figure places them: two kilograms at the origin, three kilograms four metres along the x-axis, and five kilograms three metres up the y-axis. Their balance point is the red dot we are about to compute.
Write down the givens. The masses are two, three, and five kilograms, so the total mass is ten kilograms. Always sum the mass first.
Apply the component formula. The x of the centre of mass is the mass-weighted sum of the x-coordinates over the total mass, and likewise for the y.
For x, only the three-kilogram mass has a non-zero x. Three times four is twelve, over ten, giving one point two metres.
For y, only the five-kilogram mass has a non-zero y. Five times three is fifteen, over ten, giving one point five metres.
So the centre of mass sits at one point two metres, one point five metres. Two short lines, and we are done.
And a quick sanity check: on the vertical axis the point leans up toward the heavier five-kilogram mass, exactly as mass-weighting demands.
Formula पक्का करने के लिए एक साफ़ board-level example। तीन point masses — two, three और five kilograms — तीन corners पर हैं, और हमें उनके centre of mass के coordinates चाहिए।
Figure उन्हें रखती है — two kilograms origin पर, three kilograms x-axis पर four metres, और five kilograms y-axis पर three metres ऊपर। उनका balance point वही red dot है जो हम अभी निकालेंगे।
Givens लिख लो। Masses two, three और five kilograms हैं, तो total mass ten kilograms। Mass हमेशा पहले जोड़ो।
Component formula लगाओ। Centre of mass का x है x-coordinates का mass-weighted sum बटा total mass, और वैसे ही y के लिए।
x के लिए सिर्फ़ three-kilogram mass का x non-zero है। Three गुणा four है twelve, बटा ten, मिलता है one point two metres।
y के लिए सिर्फ़ five-kilogram mass का y non-zero है। Five गुणा three है fifteen, बटा ten, मिलता है one point five metres।
तो centre of mass बैठता है one point two metres, one point five metres पर। दो छोटी lines, और काम पूरा।
और एक झटपट sanity check — vertical axis पर point भारी five-kilogram mass की ओर ऊपर झुकता है, ठीक जैसा mass-weighting माँगता है।

board_events.text: Trap: the man does not simply move 5 m; the boat slides back.
No external horizontal force, so the CoM cannot move horizontally.
The boat moves 3 m opposite to the man.
Sanity: heavier mover, bigger recoil; the man is heavier, so the boat moves more than half.

segments.text: This is a beloved N E E T speed trap. A sixty-kilogram man stands at one end of a forty-kilogram boat, five metres long, floating at rest. He walks to the other end. How far does the boat move?

The figure tells the whole story. Before, the man is at one end. After he walks across, the boat has slid backward, and the reason is written in the dashed line: the centre of mass has not moved at all.
Here is the trap. Students instinctively say the man moves five metres and stop. But water resistance is negligible, so there is no external horizontal force on the man-and-boat system.
With no external horizontal force, the centre of mass cannot shift horizontally, not even a little. So as the man walks one way, the boat must slide the other way to keep that balance point fixed.
Use the mass-ratio shortcut directly. When the man walks a length L relative to the boat, the boat shifts by the man mass over the total mass, times L.
Plug in: sixty over sixty plus forty, times five. That is sixty over one hundred, times five, which equals three metres.
So the boat moves three metres, in the direction exactly opposite to the man.
<chuckle> And the sanity check is satisfying. The heavier mover forces the bigger recoil. The man outweighs the boat, so the boat slides more than half its own length.
यह एक प्यारा N E E T speed trap है। एक sixty-kilogram आदमी forty-kilogram नाव के एक सिरे पर खड़ा है, नाव five metres लंबी, शांत पानी पर तैरती। वह दूसरे सिरे तक चलता है। नाव कितना खिसकती है?
Figure पूरी कहानी कह देती है। पहले आदमी एक सिरे पर है। पार चलने के बाद नाव पीछे सरक गई है, और वजह dashed line में लिखी है — centre of mass बिलकुल नहीं हिला।
अब trap। Students सहज ही कह देते हैं कि आदमी five metres चला, बस। पर water resistance negligible है, तो man-और-boat system पर कोई external horizontal force नहीं है।
External horizontal force न होने से centre of mass horizontally ज़रा भी shift नहीं कर सकता। इसलिए जैसे ही आदमी एक तरफ़ चलता है, नाव को उस balance point को fixed रखने के लिए दूसरी तरफ़ सरकना पड़ता है।
सीधे mass-ratio shortcut लगाओ। जब आदमी नाव के relative एक length L चलता है, तो नाव खिसकती है man mass बटा total mass, गुणा L।
रखो — sixty बटा sixty plus forty, गुणा five। यानी sixty बटा one hundred, गुणा five, जो बराबर है three metres।
तो नाव three metres खिसकती है, आदमी के बिलकुल opposite दिशा में।
<chuckle> और sanity check मज़ेदार है। जो भारी चलता है वही बड़ा recoil कराता है। आदमी नाव से भारी है, इसलिए नाव अपनी आधी लंबाई से भी ज़्यादा सरकती है।

board_events.text: Negative-mass method: remaining body = full disc + a negative hole. Mass grows as $R^2$.
Part (b): remaining mass is $3m$, removed disc is $m$; place $m$ at $x_0$ so the CoM returns to O.
The added mass sits exactly where the hole was: you are filling it back.

segments.text: Step up to J E E Main. A uniform disc of radius R has a circular hole of radius R over two cut from it, the hole centred a distance R over two from the disc centre. Find the centre of mass of what remains.
Look at the figure first. The big grey disc is the full body, the dashed circle on the right is the hole, and the green dot on the left is where the remaining centre of mass will land.
The trick is the negative-mass method. Treat the remaining body as a full disc plus a negative hole. For a uniform disc, mass is proportional to area, which is proportional to radius squared.

So the full disc has mass proportional to R squared, located at x equals zero, and the hole counts as negative mass proportional to a quarter of R squared, located at x equals R over two. Write the weighted average with that minus sign in place.

Crunch it. The numerator is minus R cubed over eight, the denominator is three R squared over four, and the ratio is minus R over six. The remaining centre of mass sits at R over six from the centre, on the side away from the hole.

Part b restores the balance. The removed disc had mass m, so the remaining portion has mass three m. Place a fresh point mass m at some position x-naught so the combined centre of mass returns to the origin.
Set the weighted average to zero: three m times minus R over six, plus m times x-naught, all over four m. Solving gives x-naught equals plus R over two.
<chuckle> And that is beautifully sensible. The added mass sits exactly at the centre of the hole you removed. You are simply filling the missing mass back where it came from.
अब J E E Main पर आते हैं। Radius R की एक uniform disc में से radius R बटा two का एक circular hole काटा गया है, hole disc के centre से R बटा two दूरी पर। जो बचा उसका centre of mass निकालो।
पहले figure देखिए। बड़ी grey disc पूरी body है, दाईं ओर dashed circle hole है, और बाईं ओर green dot वहाँ है जहाँ बचा हुआ centre of mass आएगा।
Trick है negative-mass method। बची body को full disc plus एक negative hole मानो। Uniform disc के लिए mass area के proportional है, और area radius के square के।

तो full disc की mass R square के proportional है, x बराबर zero पर, और hole एक negative mass है जो R square के एक-चौथाई के proportional है, x बराबर R बटा two पर। उस minus sign के साथ weighted average लिखो।
हल करो। Numerator है minus R cube बटा eight, denominator है three R square बटा four, और ratio है minus R बटा six। बचा हुआ centre of mass, centre से R बटा six पर बैठता है, hole से उलटी तरफ़।
Part b balance वापस लाता है। हटाई गई disc की mass m थी, तो बचे हिस्से की mass three m है। एक नया point mass m किसी position x-naught पर रखो ताकि combined centre of mass origin पर लौट आए।
Weighted average को zero रखो — three m गुणा minus R बटा six, plus m गुणा x-naught, बटा four m। हल करने पर x-naught बराबर plus R बटा two।
<chuckle> और यह बहुत सुंदर तरीके से सही है। Added mass ठीक उसी hole के centre पर बैठता है जो आपने हटाया था। आप बस ग़ायब mass को वहीं वापस भर रहे हैं जहाँ से गई थी।

board_events.text: A rod on the x-axis, $0$ to $L$, with $\lambda(x) = \lambda_0\left(1 + \tfrac{x}{L}\right)$.
A uniform rod would give $0.5L$; here density grows toward $L$, so the CoM shifts right.
The physics agrees with the algebra, since $5L/9 \gt L/2$.

segments.text: Now a J E E Advanced flavour, where the density itself varies. A thin rod lies along the x-axis from zero to L, and its linear mass density is lambda-naught times one plus x over L, heavier as you move toward the far end.
The figure captures it: the shading darkens toward x equals L, so more mass lives on the right, and the red dot marks where the centre of mass will end up.
Start with the mass element. Because density varies with position, dee m is lambda-naught times one plus x over L, all times dee x.
Total mass first. Integrate that from zero to L. You get lambda-naught times L plus L over two, which is three lambda-naught L over two.
Now the first moment of mass, the integral of x dee m from zero to L. That works out to five lambda-naught L squared over six.
Divide the first moment by the mass. The lambdas cancel, the L powers simplify, and the centre of mass lands at five L over nine, about zero point five five six of the length.

Read the result against intuition. A uniform rod would balance dead centre at half of L. Here the density grows toward the far end, so the centre of mass should shift toward that heavier side, and it does.
<excited> Five L over nine is indeed greater than half of L, so the physics and the algebra shake hands. Whenever your answer agrees with a physical prediction like this, you can trust it.

अब एक J E E Advanced flavour, जहाँ density खुद बदलती है। एक पतली rod x-axis पर zero से L तक है, और उसकी linear mass density है lambda-naught गुणा one plus x बटा L, दूर वाले सिरे की ओर जितना बढ़ो उतनी भारी।
Figure इसे पकड़ती है — shading x बराबर L की ओर गहरी होती जाती है, तो ज़्यादा mass दाईं ओर बसती है, और red dot बताता है centre of mass कहाँ आएगा।
Mass element से शुरू करो। Density position के साथ बदलती है, इसलिए dee m है lambda-naught गुणा one plus x बटा L, गुणा dee x।
पहले total mass। उसे zero से L तक integrate करो। मिलता है lambda-naught गुणा L plus L बटा two, यानी three lambda-naught L बटा two।
अब mass का first moment, x dee m का integral zero से L तक। यह बनता है five lambda-naught L square बटा six।
First moment को mass से भाग दो। Lambdas cancel, L की powers simplify, और centre of mass आ जाता है five L बटा nine पर, लगभग length का zero point five five six।
Result को intuition के सामने पढ़ो। Uniform rod ठीक बीच में, L के आधे पर balance करती। यहाँ density दूर वाले सिरे की ओर बढ़ती है, तो centre of mass उस भारी तरफ़ खिसकना चाहिए, और खिसकता है।
<excited> Five L बटा nine सचमुच L के आधे से बड़ा है, तो physics और algebra हाथ मिला लेते हैं। जब भी आपका answer ऐसी physical prediction से मेल खाए, आप उस पर भरोसा कर सकते हैं।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Pitfalls that cost easy marks
1. Treating the CoM as a midpoint. It is mass-weighted; halfway is right only for equal masses.
Always lean the answer toward the heavier mass, then sanity-check that it did.
2. Confusing the semicircular wire with the semicircular disc.
Wire (arc) gives $\dfrac{2R}{\pi}$; filled disc gives $\dfrac{4R}{3\pi}$. Examiners offer both.
3. Forgetting that internal forces do not move the CoM: anchor to it in explosions and recoil.
4. Sign errors in the negative-mass method: the removed piece is negative in numerator and denominator.
Pro-tip: use the ratio form; the CoM always shifts away from the hole, so a direction check catches half of all sign slips.

segments.text: Let us close the centre of mass with the four traps examiners set again and again, and the pro-tips that defuse them.
Trap one: treating the centre of mass as a simple midpoint. It is a mass-weighted average, not a geometric one. Exactly halfway is correct only when the masses are equal.
So always lean your answer toward the heavier mass, then sanity-check that it actually did. That single reflex catches a surprising number of slips.
Trap two, the deadliest: confusing the semicircular wire with the semicircular disc. Examiners deliberately place both on the option list to catch you.
<whisper> Tattoo this into memory. The wire, an arc, gives two R over pi. The filled disc gives four R over three pi. Different objects, different answers.
Trap three: forgetting that internal forces cannot move the centre of mass. In explosions, recoil, and man-on-boat problems, anchor to the centre of mass first and the rest falls into place.

Trap four: sign errors in the negative-mass method. The removed piece contributes a negative mass in both the numerator and the denominator. Drop one sign and your centre of mass flips to the wrong side.

And the pro-tip that ties it together. For removed-portion problems, use the ratio form and remember the centre of mass always shifts away from the hole. A quick direction check before you compute catches half of all sign mistakes, and on N E E T that is thirty seconds saved per question.
Centre of mass को उन चार traps के साथ बंद करते हैं जो examiners बार-बार लगाते हैं, और उन pro-tips के साथ जो इन्हें निष्क्रिय कर देते हैं।
Trap one — centre of mass को सीधा midpoint मान लेना। यह mass-weighted average है, geometric नहीं। ठीक बीच में तभी सही है जब masses बराबर हों।
तो answer को हमेशा भारी mass की ओर झुकाओ, फिर check करो कि सचमुच झुका या नहीं। यही एक reflex हैरान करने वाली कई ग़लतियाँ पकड़ लेता है।
Trap two, सबसे घातक — semicircular wire को semicircular disc से confuse करना। Examiners जान-बूझकर दोनों को options में रखते हैं ताकि आप फँसें।
<whisper> इसे याददाश्त में गुदवा लो। Wire यानी arc देता है two R बटा pi। भरी हुई disc देती है four R बटा three pi। अलग objects, अलग answers।
Trap three — यह भूल जाना कि internal forces centre of mass को नहीं हिला सकते। Explosions, recoil और man-on-boat problems में पहले centre of mass को anchor करो, बाक़ी अपने आप बैठ जाता है।
Trap four — negative-mass method में sign errors। हटाया गया टुकड़ा numerator और denominator दोनों में negative mass देता है। एक sign छूटा और centre of mass ग़लत तरफ़ पलट जाता है।

और वह pro-tip जो सब जोड़ता है। Removed-portion problems में ratio form इस्तेमाल करो और याद रखो कि centre of mass हमेशा hole से दूर खिसकता है। Compute करने से पहले एक झटपट direction check आधी sign mistakes पकड़ लेता है, और N E E T में वह हर question पर thirty seconds की बचत है।

board_events.text: Dot product asks: how much do two vectors point the same way? It returns a scalar.
Cross product asks: how much do they point in different directions, and which way does their plane face?
Remarkably, the cross product returns a vector.
Opening a door: push at a distance from the hinge, and the door turns about an axis perpendicular to both.
Right-hand rule: sweep the first vector to the second; the thumb gives the product direction.
Magnitude equals the parallelogram area: largest when perpendicular, zero when parallel.

segments.text: <curious> You already know one way to multiply two vectors, the dot product. Here is a second, completely different way, and it is the mathematical engine behind torque and angular momentum for the rest of this chapter.
Keep this figure in view. Two vectors A and B lie in a plane, they span a parallelogram, and their cross product points straight out of that plane.
The dot product asks: how much do two vectors point the same way? Its answer is a plain number, a scalar.
The cross product asks a different question entirely: how much do the two vectors point in different directions, and which way is the plane they define facing?
And here is the surprise: the answer to that question is itself a vector, not a number. Some physical quantities genuinely need a direction perpendicular to two given directions at once.

Think of opening a door. You push at some distance from the hinge, and the door swings about an axis perpendicular to both your push and the line to the hinge. That axis is exactly what the cross product captures.

To find its direction, use the right-hand rule: sweep the fingers of your right hand from the first vector toward the second, and your thumb points along the product. That rule is the whole geometric soul of the operation.

Its magnitude has a lovely meaning too: it equals the area of the parallelogram built on A and B. That area is largest when the vectors are perpendicular and shrinks to zero when they are parallel, so the cross product measures how perpendicular two vectors are.

<curious> आप already दो vectors को multiply करने का एक तरीक़ा जानते हैं, dot product। यहाँ एक दूसरा, बिलकुल अलग तरीक़ा है, और यही इस chapter के आगे torque और angular momentum का mathematical engine है।
इस figure को सामने रखिए। दो vectors A और B एक plane में हैं, वे एक parallelogram बनाते हैं, और उनका cross product उस plane से सीधे बाहर की ओर point करता है।
Dot product पूछता है — दो vectors कितना एक ही दिशा में point करते हैं? उसका answer एक सादा number है, एक scalar।
Cross product बिलकुल अलग सवाल पूछता है — दो vectors कितना अलग-अलग दिशाओं में point करते हैं, और जो plane वे बनाते हैं वह किस ओर मुँह किए है?
और यहाँ surprise है — उस सवाल का answer खुद एक vector है, number नहीं। कुछ physical quantities को सचमुच एक ऐसी direction चाहिए जो एक साथ दो दी हुई directions के perpendicular हो।

दरवाज़ा खोलने की सोचिए। आप hinge से कुछ दूरी पर push करते हैं, और दरवाज़ा एक ऐसे axis के बारे में घूमता है जो आपके push और hinge तक की line, दोनों के perpendicular है। वही axis cross product पकड़ता है।
इसकी direction के लिए right-hand rule लगाओ — अपने दाहिने हाथ की fingers पहले vector से दूसरे की ओर sweep करो, और thumb product की दिशा बताता है। यही rule इस operation की पूरी geometric आत्मा है।

इसकी magnitude का भी सुंदर अर्थ है — यह A और B पर बने parallelogram के area के बराबर है। वह area तब सबसे बड़ा है जब vectors perpendicular हों, और zero तब जब parallel, यानी cross product मापता है कि दो vectors कितने perpendicular हैं।

<text x="204" y="116" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#2f7d5a">B</text>
<line x1="150" y1="150" x2="150" y2="55" stroke="#2b6ca3" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#acU)"/>
<text x="90" y="60" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#2b6ca3">A cross B</text>
<line x1="150" y1="150" x2="150" y2="225" stroke="#b3402f" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#acD)"/>
<text x="160" y="215" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#b3402f">B cross A (flipped)</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Rule one: the cross product is defined only in three dimensions.
Rule two: it is anti-commutative. $\vec A \times \vec B = -\,\vec B \times \vec A$.
Swap the order and the thumb points the opposite way; the result flips sign.
Rule three: parallel or anti-parallel vectors give zero, since $\sin\theta = 0$.
In particular, any vector crossed with itself is the zero vector.
These three rules quietly decide clockwise versus anticlockwise in every torque problem ahead.

segments.text: Before the formulas, lock in three ground rules. Break any of them and a torque answer flips to the wrong sense in an exam.
The figure shows the key one. The same two vectors give A cross B pointing up, but B cross A pointing straight down, equal in size, opposite in direction.
Rule one: the cross product is defined only in three dimensions. The dot product works in any number of dimensions, but the perpendicular-direction idea needs three-dimensional space to live in.
Rule two, the one the figure captures: the cross product is anti-commutative. A cross B equals minus B cross A. This is unlike ordinary multiplication and unlike the dot product.
Why? Because swapping the vectors makes your right-hand thumb point the opposite way. The magnitude is unchanged, but the direction, and so the sign, flips completely.
Rule three: parallel or anti-parallel vectors give zero. If A lies along B, the angle between them is zero or one hundred eighty degrees, the sine of that is zero, so the cross product vanishes.
As a special case, any vector crossed with itself is the zero vector, because a vector is certainly parallel to itself.
<curious> These three rules look small, but they quietly decide clockwise versus anticlockwise in every torque and angular-momentum problem for the rest of the chapter.
Formulas से पहले तीन ground rules पक्की कर लो। इनमें से कोई भी टूटी, तो exam में torque का answer ग़लत sense में पलट जाता है।
Figure सबसे अहम rule दिखाती है। वही दो vectors A cross B को ऊपर point कराते हैं, पर B cross A को सीधे नीचे, size में बराबर, direction में opposite।
Rule one — cross product सिर्फ़ three dimensions में defined है। Dot product किसी भी number of dimensions में चलता है, पर perpendicular-direction का idea जीने के लिए three-dimensional space चाहिए।
Rule two, जो figure पकड़ती है — cross product anti-commutative है। A cross B बराबर minus B cross A। यह ordinary multiplication और dot product, दोनों से अलग है।
क्यों? क्योंकि vectors की order बदलते ही आपके right-hand का thumb उलटी ओर point करता है। Magnitude वही रहती है, पर direction, और इसलिए sign, पूरी तरह पलट जाता है।
Rule three — parallel या anti-parallel vectors zero देते हैं। अगर A, B के साथ हो, तो उनके बीच का angle zero या one hundred eighty degrees है, उसका sine zero है, इसलिए cross product ग़ायब हो जाता है।
एक special case के तौर पर, कोई भी vector खुद से cross करने पर zero vector देता है, क्योंकि vector खुद के तो parallel है ही।
<curious> ये तीन rules छोटे लगते हैं, पर chapter के आगे हर torque और angular-momentum problem में clockwise बनाम anticlockwise ये ही चुपचाप तय करते हैं।

board_events.latex: \vec A \times \vec B = -\,\vec B \times \vec A,\qquad \vec A \times \vec A = \vec 0
\hat i \times \hat j = \hat k,\quad \hat j \times \hat k = \hat i,\quad \hat k \times \hat i = \hat j
\vec A \times \vec B = \begin{vmatrix}\hat i & \hat j & \hat k\\ A_x & A_y & A_z\\ B_x & B_y & B_z\end{vmatrix}

board_events.text: Area of parallelogram $=|\vec A\times\vec B|$; triangle $=\tfrac12|\vec A\times\vec B|$.

board_events.latex: |\vec A \times \vec B|^2 + (\vec A \cdot \vec B)^2 = A^2 B^2

segments.text: Here is the full cross-product toolkit. Every vector-product problem is one of these lines in disguise.
First the memory aid in the figure. The unit vectors run around a ring: i to j to k and back to i. Go forward around the ring and the product is positive; go backward and you pick up a minus sign.
The defining formula: A cross B equals A times B times sine theta, all along the unit vector n-hat that is perpendicular to both, in the right-hand-rule sense.
Strip away the direction and the magnitude alone is A times B times sine theta.
Two core properties to keep close: the product is anti-commutative, so A cross B is minus B cross A, and any vector crossed with itself is the zero vector.
The unit-vector products follow the ring: i cross j is k, j cross k is i, and k cross i is j. Reverse any of these and the sign flips.

<excited> For vectors given in components, the workhorse is the determinant. Write i, j, k across the top, the first vector in the middle row, the second in the bottom row, and expand, remembering the minus sign on the j term.
Two geometric payoffs: the magnitude of A cross B is the area of the parallelogram on A and B, and half of it is the area of the triangle.
And a neat identity linking the two products: the magnitude of the cross squared plus the dot squared equals A squared times B squared. Cross and dot carry complementary information.
यह रहा पूरा cross-product toolkit। हर vector-product problem इन्हीं lines में से किसी एक का रूप है।
पहले figure वाला memory aid। Unit vectors एक ring में घूमते हैं — i से j, j से k, और वापस i। Ring में आगे जाओ तो product positive; पीछे जाओ तो एक minus sign लग जाता है।
Defining formula — A cross B बराबर A गुणा B गुणा sine theta, उस unit vector n-hat के साथ जो दोनों के perpendicular है, right-hand-rule के sense में।
Direction हटा दो तो अकेली magnitude है A गुणा B गुणा sine theta।
दो core properties पास रखो — product anti-commutative है, तो A cross B बराबर minus B cross A, और कोई भी vector खुद से cross करने पर zero vector।
Unit-vector products ring को follow करते हैं — i cross j बराबर k, j cross k बराबर i, और k cross i बराबर j। इनमें से किसी को उलटो तो sign पलट जाता है।
<excited> Components में दिए vectors के लिए workhorse है determinant। ऊपर i, j, k लिखो, बीच row में पहला vector, नीचे row में दूसरा, और expand करो, j term पर minus sign याद रखते हुए।
दो geometric फ़ायदे — A cross B की magnitude, A और B पर बने parallelogram का area है, और उसका आधा triangle का area।
और दोनों products को जोड़ने वाली एक साफ़ identity — cross की magnitude का square plus dot का square बराबर A square गुणा B square। Cross और dot एक-दूसरे की पूरक जानकारी रखते हैं।

sections.title: Why the result is perpendicular, and how to compute it

board_events.text: Why the result is perpendicular, and how to compute it

board_events.caption: i, j, k on top; first vector middle, second bottom
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 220" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="420" height="220" fill="#ffffff"/>
<text x="210" y="28" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#22303c">The determinant is the workhorse</text>
<line x1="120" y1="55" x2="120" y2="175" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="2"/>
<line x1="330" y1="55" x2="330" y2="175" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="150" y="85" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#2b6ca3">i</text><text x="215" y="85" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#b3402f">j</text><text x="285" y="85" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#2b6ca3">k</text>
<text x="145" y="125" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#c2820a">Ax</text><text x="210" y="125" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#c2820a">Ay</text><text x="280" y="125" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#c2820a">Az</text>
<text x="145" y="162" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#2f7d5a">Bx</text><text x="210" y="162" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#2f7d5a">By</text><text x="280" y="162" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#2f7d5a">Bz</text>
<text x="210" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#b3402f">remember the minus sign on the j term</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Let $\vec C = \vec A \times \vec B$ from the determinant expansion.

board_events.latex: \vec A \cdot \vec C = A_x(A_yB_z - A_zB_y) + A_y(A_zB_x - A_xB_z) + A_z(A_xB_y - A_yB_x)

board_events.text: Every term cancels in a plus-minus pair, so $\vec A \cdot \vec C = 0$: $\vec C$ is perpendicular to $\vec A$.
Procedure: write the determinant, expand along the top row with the minus on the j term.
Sanity step: dot your answer with either original vector; you must get zero.
For two vectors in the xy-plane, only the k-term survives: $A_xB_y - A_yB_x$.

segments.text: Why does the cross product come out perpendicular to both vectors? Let us actually prove it, and pick up the computing procedure along the way.
Set up the determinant as in the figure: i, j, k across the top, the first vector in the middle row, the second in the bottom row. Call the resulting vector C.
To test whether C is perpendicular to A, dot the two together. If the dot product is zero, they are perpendicular by definition.
Write out A dot C using the components of C from the determinant. You get a sum of six terms, each a product of three components.

Now watch them cancel. Every term is matched by an equal term with the opposite sign, for instance A-x A-y B-z cancels minus A-y A-x B-z. The whole sum collapses to zero, so C is perpendicular to A, and by the same algebra, perpendicular to B.

That gives the procedure. Write the determinant, then expand along the top row, always remembering the minus sign sitting on the middle, j term. That single sign is the most common slip in the whole topic.
Then take the sanity step every time: dot your answer with either original vector. You must get zero. This one check, costing five seconds, catches almost every arithmetic error.
<whisper> And a shortcut worth memorising: when both vectors already lie in the xy-plane, only the k-component survives, and it is simply A-x B-y minus A-y B-x. Skip the full determinant entirely.
Cross product दोनों vectors के perpendicular क्यों निकलता है? इसे सचमुच prove करते हैं, और साथ में computing procedure भी उठा लेते हैं।
Figure की तरह determinant set करो — ऊपर i, j, k, बीच row में पहला vector, नीचे row में दूसरा। परिणामी vector को C कहो।
यह test करने के लिए कि C, A के perpendicular है या नहीं, दोनों को dot करो। अगर dot product zero है, तो वे definition से perpendicular हैं।
A dot C को C के components से लिखो, जो determinant से आए। छह terms का एक sum मिलता है, हर एक तीन components का product।

अब इन्हें cancel होते देखो। हर term का एक बराबर term है opposite sign के साथ, जैसे A-x A-y B-z, minus A-y A-x B-z से cancel। पूरा sum zero पर सिमट जाता है, तो C, A के perpendicular है, और उसी algebra से B के भी।
इससे procedure मिलती है। Determinant लिखो, फिर top row के साथ expand करो, बीच वाले j term पर बैठे minus sign को हमेशा याद रखते हुए। वही एक sign पूरे topic की सबसे आम ग़लती है।
फिर हर बार sanity step लो — अपने answer को किसी एक original vector से dot करो। zero आना ही चाहिए। पाँच second का यह एक check लगभग हर arithmetic error पकड़ लेता है।
<whisper> और एक shortcut याद रखने लायक़ — जब दोनों vectors पहले से xy-plane में हों, तो सिर्फ़ k-component बचता है, जो बस A-x B-y minus A-y B-x है। पूरा determinant छोड़ ही दो।

board_events.text: Compute $\vec A \times \vec B$ [CBSE Board]

board_events.caption: Rows 2 3 1 and 1 minus 1 2; result and check

</svg>

board_events.text: $\vec A = 2\hat i + 3\hat j + \hat k$, $\vec B = \hat i - \hat j + 2\hat k$.

board_events.latex: = \hat i(6+1) - \hat j(4-1) + \hat k(-2-3) = 7\hat i - 3\hat j - 5\hat k

board_events.text: The zero check confirms the answer is perpendicular to $\vec A$.
Answer: $\vec A \times \vec B = 7\hat i - 3\hat j - 5\hat k$.

segments.text: A clean board-level computation to drill the determinant. Cross the vector A, which is two i plus three j plus k, with B, which is i minus j plus two k.
The figure lays out the grid: i, j, k on top, the row two, three, one for A, and the row one, minus one, two for B.
Write those givens carefully; one sign wrong in B and everything downstream fails.
Set up the determinant with i, j, k across the top and the two component rows below.

Expand across the top row. The i term is three times two minus one times minus one, which is six plus one, so seven. The j term, with its minus, is two times two minus one, which is three, so minus three j. The k term is two times minus one minus three, which is minus five. The result is seven i minus three j minus five k.

<excited> Now the compulsory check. Dot A with the answer: two times seven is fourteen, plus three times minus three is minus nine, plus one times minus five is minus five. Fourteen minus nine minus five is zero.
That zero is your guarantee: the answer is genuinely perpendicular to A, so the arithmetic held up.
So the cross product is seven i minus three j minus five k. Board marks secured, with a built-in proof that it is right.
Determinant पक्का करने के लिए एक साफ़ board-level computation। Vector A — two i plus three j plus k — को B — i minus j plus two k — से cross करो।
Figure grid बिछाती है — ऊपर i, j, k, A के लिए row two, three, one, और B के लिए row one, minus one, two।
इन givens को ध्यान से लिखो; B में एक sign ग़लत और आगे सब कुछ बिगड़ जाता है।
Determinant set करो, ऊपर i, j, k और नीचे दो component rows।

Top row के साथ expand करो। i term है three गुणा two minus one गुणा minus one, यानी six plus one, तो seven। j term, अपने minus के साथ, है two गुणा two minus one, यानी three, तो minus three j। k term है two गुणा minus one minus three, यानी minus five। result है seven i minus three j minus five k।

<excited> अब अनिवार्य check। A को answer से dot करो — two गुणा seven है fourteen, plus three गुणा minus three है minus nine, plus one गुणा minus five है minus five। Fourteen minus nine minus five बराबर zero।
वह zero आपकी guarantee है — answer सचमुच A के perpendicular है, यानी arithmetic सही रही।
तो cross product है seven i minus three j minus five k। Board के marks पक्के, और साथ में built-in proof कि सही है।

board_events.text: Trap: no need for the full vector machinery; only magnitudes matter.
Given magnitudes 6 and 5, with $|\vec A \times \vec B| = 15$.
Sanity: the maximum product is $6\times 5 = 30$ at ninety degrees; we got exactly half.
So a thirty-degree angle fits perfectly.

segments.text: A quick N E E T speed trap. Two vectors have magnitudes six and five units, and the magnitude of their cross product is fifteen. Find the angle between them.
The figure holds the only relationship you need: the magnitude of A cross B equals A times B times sine theta.
Here is the trap. Students set up the full vector machinery, components and determinants. But only the magnitudes are asked for, so reach straight for that magnitude formula.
Write the givens: the magnitudes are six and five, and the cross-product magnitude is fifteen.
Substitute: fifteen equals six times five, times sine theta. That is thirty sine theta, so sine theta is fifteen over thirty, which is one half.
Sine theta equals one half gives theta equal to thirty degrees.
Sanity-check against the maximum. The largest the product could ever be is six times five, that is thirty, reached at ninety degrees. We got exactly half of that.
<chuckle> Half the maximum means sine theta is one half, and a thirty-degree angle fits perfectly. One line, no determinant.
एक झटपट N E E T speed trap। दो vectors की magnitudes six और five units हैं, और उनके cross product की magnitude fifteen है। उनके बीच का angle निकालो।
Figure में वही एक relationship है जो चाहिए — A cross B की magnitude बराबर A गुणा B गुणा sine theta।
यहाँ trap है। Students पूरी vector machinery — components और determinants — set कर बैठते हैं। पर पूछी सिर्फ़ magnitudes गई हैं, तो सीधे उस magnitude formula पर जाओ।
Givens लिखो — magnitudes six और five, और cross-product magnitude fifteen।
Substitute करो — fifteen बराबर six गुणा five, गुणा sine theta। यानी thirty sine theta, तो sine theta है fifteen बटा thirty, जो one half है।
Sine theta बराबर one half देता है theta बराबर thirty degrees।
Maximum के सामने sanity-check। Product ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा six गुणा five यानी thirty हो सकता है, ninety degrees पर। हमें ठीक उसका आधा मिला।
<chuckle> Maximum का आधा मतलब sine theta है one half, और thirty-degree का angle बिलकुल fit बैठता है। एक line, कोई determinant नहीं।

board_events.text: $\vec P = 3\hat i + \hat j$, $\vec Q = \hat i + 4\hat j$ are two sides of a triangle.

board_events.latex: \hat n = \frac{\vec P \times \vec Q}{|\vec P \times \vec Q|} = \frac{11\hat k}{11} = \hat k

board_events.text: Both sides lie in the xy-plane, so the perpendicular points along the z-axis.
Answer: area $= 5.5$ square units; perpendicular unit vector $= \hat k$.

segments.text: Now a J E E Main problem that blends two ideas at once, the area interpretation and the perpendicular-direction use. The sides of a triangle are the vectors P and Q.
The figure shows both sides lying flat in the xy-plane, so their cross product must stick straight up along the z-axis.
Write the sides: P is three i plus j, and Q is i plus four j. Both have zero z-component.
Because both lie in the xy-plane, only the k-component of the cross product survives. It is three times four minus one times one, which is twelve minus one, so eleven k.
The area of the triangle is half the magnitude of that cross product. Half of eleven is five point five square units.
For the perpendicular direction, divide the cross product by its own magnitude. Eleven k over eleven is simply k-hat, a clean unit vector.
And that makes complete sense: both sides lie in the xy-plane, so the direction perpendicular to the plane points along the z-axis.
<excited> So the area is five point five square units and the perpendicular unit vector is k-hat. Two J E E Main skills answered from one cross product.
अब एक J E E Main problem जो एक साथ दो ideas मिलाती है — area interpretation और perpendicular-direction का इस्तेमाल। एक triangle की sides हैं vectors P और Q।
Figure दिखाती है कि दोनों sides xy-plane में सपाट पड़ी हैं, तो उनका cross product सीधे z-axis के साथ ऊपर खड़ा होना चाहिए।
Sides लिखो — P है three i plus j, और Q है i plus four j। दोनों का z-component zero है।
क्योंकि दोनों xy-plane में हैं, cross product का सिर्फ़ k-component बचता है। वह है three गुणा four minus one गुणा one, यानी twelve minus one, तो eleven k।
Triangle का area उस cross product की magnitude का आधा है। Eleven का आधा है five point five square units।
Perpendicular direction के लिए cross product को उसकी अपनी magnitude से भाग दो। Eleven k बटा eleven बस k-hat है, एक साफ़ unit vector।
और यह पूरी तरह sense बनाता है — दोनों sides xy-plane में हैं, तो plane के perpendicular direction z-axis के साथ point करती है।
<excited> तो area है five point five square units और perpendicular unit vector है k-hat। एक ही cross product से दो J E E Main skills हल।

board_events.text: $\vec X$ in the xy-plane with $\vec X \times (2\hat i + 3\hat j) = 6\hat k$ and $\vec X \cdot (2\hat i + 3\hat j) = 0$.
Dot fixes the direction (perpendicular); cross fixes the magnitude and sense.

segments.text: A J E E Advanced twist: instead of computing a cross product, we solve for an unknown vector using both a dot and a cross condition together.
The figure captures the logic. The unknown X lies in the xy-plane and must be perpendicular to two i plus three j, and the cross condition then fixes its exact length and sense.
Write X as x i plus y j. The two given conditions become two simultaneous equations.
First, the dot product with two i plus three j is zero. That gives two x plus three y equals zero, call it equation one. This is what forces X to be perpendicular.
Second, the cross product equals six k. For two planar vectors, the cross is the k-term x times three minus y times two, so three x minus two y equals six, equation two.
Solve them together. From equation one, x is minus three halves y. Substitute into equation two to get minus thirteen halves y equals six, so y is minus twelve over thirteen.
Back-substitute for x, which comes out to eighteen over thirteen. So X is eighteen over thirteen i minus twelve over thirteen j.

<curious> Notice the division of labour: the dot product fixed the direction by demanding perpendicularity, while the cross product fixed the magnitude and sense. Dot and cross encode complementary information.
एक J E E Advanced twist — cross product निकालने के बजाय, हम एक unknown vector के लिए dot और cross condition, दोनों को साथ इस्तेमाल करके हल करते हैं।
Figure logic पकड़ती है। Unknown X, xy-plane में है और two i plus three j के perpendicular होना चाहिए, और फिर cross condition उसकी ठीक length और sense तय करती है।
X को x i plus y j लिखो। दोनों दी हुई conditions दो simultaneous equations बन जाती हैं।
पहली — two i plus three j के साथ dot product zero है। इससे मिलता है two x plus three y बराबर zero, इसे equation one कहो। यही X को perpendicular होने पर मजबूर करती है।
दूसरी — cross product बराबर six k। दो planar vectors के लिए cross वही k-term है x गुणा three minus y गुणा two, तो three x minus two y बराबर six, equation two।
इन्हें साथ हल करो। Equation one से x है minus three halves y। Equation two में substitute करो तो minus thirteen halves y बराबर six, यानी y है minus twelve बटा thirteen।
x के लिए back-substitute करो, जो निकलता है eighteen बटा thirteen। तो X है eighteen बटा thirteen i minus twelve बटा thirteen j।
<curious> काम का बँटवारा देखिए — dot product ने perpendicularity माँगकर direction तय की, जबकि cross product ने magnitude और sense तय की। Dot और cross एक-दूसरे की पूरक जानकारी रखते हैं।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Cross-product traps that cost marks
1. Treating the cross product like ordinary multiplication; it is anti-commutative.
Reversing the order flips the sign: costly in torque, where direction sets clockwise versus anticlockwise.
2. Forgetting the minus sign on the j term in the determinant expansion.
3. Confusing dot and cross: dot uses cosine, maximal when parallel; cross uses sine, maximal when perpendicular.
4. Believing parallel vectors give a non-zero product; parallel means $\sin\theta = 0$, so zero.
That is why a force pushing straight toward a hinge produces no torque.
Pro-tip: after any cross product, dot the result with an original vector; if it is not zero, redo it.

segments.text: Let us close the vector product with the four traps examiners rely on, and the one habit that defuses most of them.
Trap one: treating the cross product like ordinary multiplication. It is anti-commutative, A cross B equals minus B cross A.
Reversing the order flips the sign, and that is genuinely costly in torque problems, where the direction is exactly what decides clockwise versus anticlockwise.
Trap two, the single most common cross-product mistake in exams: forgetting the minus sign on the middle, j term when you expand the determinant.

Trap three: confusing the dot and the cross. The dot gives a scalar and uses cosine, so it is largest when the vectors are parallel. The cross gives a vector and uses sine, so it is largest when they are perpendicular. Mixing them up corrupts the whole solution.
Trap four: believing parallel vectors give a non-zero product. Parallel means the angle is zero, the sine is zero, so the cross product is zero.
And that fact has a physical face you will meet next: a force pushing straight toward a hinge produces no torque at all.

<whisper> The pro-tip that ties it together: after any cross-product calculation, dot the result with one of the original vectors. If you do not get zero, you made an arithmetic error, so go back. Five seconds spent, whole questions saved.
Vector product को उन चार traps के साथ बंद करते हैं जिन पर examiners भरोसा करते हैं, और उस एक आदत के साथ जो ज़्यादातर को निष्क्रिय कर देती है।
Trap one — cross product को ordinary multiplication की तरह मानना। यह anti-commutative है, A cross B बराबर minus B cross A।
Order उलटने से sign पलट जाता है, और torque problems में यह सचमुच महँगा है, जहाँ direction ही तय करती है clockwise बनाम anticlockwise।
Trap two, exams की सबसे आम cross-product ग़लती — determinant expand करते समय बीच वाले j term पर minus sign भूल जाना।

Trap three — dot और cross को confuse करना। Dot एक scalar देता है और cosine use करता है, तो parallel पर सबसे बड़ा। Cross एक vector देता है और sine use करता है, तो perpendicular पर सबसे बड़ा। इन्हें मिला दो तो पूरा solution बिगड़ जाता है।
Trap four — यह मानना कि parallel vectors non-zero product देते हैं। Parallel मतलब angle zero, sine zero, तो cross product zero।
और इस बात का एक physical रूप आगे मिलेगा — hinge की सीधी ओर धकेलता force बिलकुल कोई torque नहीं बनाता।

<whisper> वह pro-tip जो सब जोड़ता है — किसी भी cross-product calculation के बाद, result को किसी एक original vector से dot करो। अगर zero न मिले, तो arithmetic error हुई है, वापस जाओ। पाँच second लगे, पूरे questions बचे।

board_events.text: Torque depends on three things: how hard, how far from the pivot, and in which direction you push.
Only the force component perpendicular to the pivot-to-push line turns the body.
A force aimed straight at the axis has zero turning effect.
A mechanic grabs the longest spanner and pushes at right angles for maximum torque.
A couple: two equal, opposite, non-collinear forces; torque $= F\times d$, pure rotation.
Torque is an axial vector: the right-hand rule gives its direction along the axis.

segments.text: <curious> Think about the last time you opened a heavy door. You pushed on the handle, the edge farthest from the hinges, never near the hinge, because that feels useless. That instinct is the whole concept of torque living in your muscle memory.
The figure shows both moves. A push perpendicular to the door, far from the hinge, produces a big turn. A push aimed straight at the hinge produces nothing at all.
Torque is the turning effect of a force, and it depends on three things: how hard you push, how far from the pivot you push, and in which direction you push. The door teaches all three.
Here is the point students forget. Only the part of the force perpendicular to the line joining the pivot and the push actually turns the body.
A force aimed straight at the axis has zero turning effect, no matter how hard you shove. Push toward the hinge and the door does not budge.
This is why a mechanic loosening a tight bolt grabs the longest spanner and pushes at right angles to it: maximum distance and maximum perpendicular force give maximum torque.

One special case worth naming is a couple: two equal, opposite, parallel forces whose lines do not coincide, like two hands turning a steering wheel. A couple gives pure rotation with no net force, and its torque is simply the force times the perpendicular distance between them.

Finally, a word on direction. Torque is an axial vector; it points along the rotation axis, not in the plane of motion. Curl the fingers of your right hand in the sense of rotation, and your thumb points along the torque.

<curious> पिछली बार जब आपने कोई भारी दरवाज़ा खोला था, याद कीजिए। आपने handle पर push किया, hinges से सबसे दूर वाले किनारे पर, hinge के पास कभी नहीं, क्योंकि वह बेकार लगता है। यही instinct torque की पूरी concept है, आपकी muscle memory में बसी।
Figure दोनों moves दिखाती है। दरवाज़े के perpendicular, hinge से दूर push बड़ा turn बनाता है। सीधे hinge की ओर push कुछ भी नहीं करता।
Torque किसी force का turning effect है, और यह तीन चीज़ों पर निर्भर करता है — कितना ज़ोर, pivot से कितनी दूर, और किस direction में push। दरवाज़ा तीनों सिखाता है।
यहाँ वह बात है जो students भूल जाते हैं। सिर्फ़ force का वह हिस्सा जो pivot और push को जोड़ने वाली line के perpendicular है, body को turn करता है।
Axis की सीधी ओर ताका गया force zero turning effect देता है, चाहे कितना भी ज़ोर लगाओ। Hinge की ओर push करो और दरवाज़ा टस से मस नहीं होता।
इसीलिए एक mechanic tight bolt खोलते समय सबसे लंबा spanner पकड़ता है और उसके right angles पर push करता है — maximum distance और maximum perpendicular force मिलकर maximum torque देते हैं।

एक special case नाम लेने लायक़ है — couple: दो बराबर, opposite, parallel forces जिनकी lines मिलती नहीं, जैसे steering wheel घुमाते दो हाथ। Couple बिना net force के pure rotation देता है, और उसका torque बस force गुणा उनके बीच की perpendicular distance है।

आख़िर में direction की बात। Torque एक axial vector है; यह rotation axis के साथ point करता है, motion के plane में नहीं। अपने दाहिने हाथ की fingers rotation के sense में मोड़ो, और thumb torque की दिशा बताता है।

board_events.text: Angular momentum $\vec L$ is the rotational cousin of linear momentum $\vec p$.
Like linear momentum it resists change: a spinning top stays upright, a moving bicycle is easy to balance.
A dancer pulls her arms in, shrinking $I$; with $L = I\omega$ fixed, $\omega$ shoots up.
Kepler second law is angular-momentum conservation: a planet speeds up near the Sun.
A collapsing star becomes a neutron star spinning hundreds of times per second, by the same law.
Conservation holds only when the net external torque is zero; internal forces only rearrange $I$ and $\omega$.

segments.text: If torque is the rotational cousin of force, then angular momentum is the rotational cousin of linear momentum. It is the quantity of rotational motion stored in a spinning body.
The figure shows the most famous demonstration. A dancer spins with arms outstretched, then pulls them in, and suddenly whips around far faster, though no one pushed her.
Angular momentum, written L, plays the same role for rotation that ordinary momentum p plays for straight-line motion.

And like linear momentum, it resists being changed. A spinning top stays upright, a moving bicycle is far easier to balance than a stationary one, and a spun cricket ball holds its line, all because angular momentum is locked in.

Back to the dancer. She pulls her arms in, which shrinks her moment of inertia. Since angular momentum, the moment of inertia times omega, must stay constant with no external torque, shrinking the moment of inertia forces omega to shoot up. Arms in, spin faster.

The same law runs the heavens. A planet feels a force always directed toward the Sun, which has zero torque about the Sun, so its angular momentum is conserved. That is why it speeds up when it swings close and slows when far, Kepler second law in disguise.

<excited> Push it further and you get one of the most dramatic events in physics. When a giant star collapses into a tiny neutron star, its moment of inertia plummets, and to conserve angular momentum its spin rate explodes; some neutron stars rotate hundreds of times per second.

One caution that decides exam questions: this conservation holds only when the net external torque is zero. Internal forces, like the dancer muscles, can rearrange the moment of inertia and omega, but can never change the total angular momentum.
अगर torque force का rotational cousin है, तो angular momentum linear momentum का rotational cousin है। यह किसी spinning body में जमा rotational motion की मात्रा है।
Figure सबसे मशहूर demonstration दिखाती है। एक dancer बाहें फैलाकर घूमती है, फिर उन्हें अंदर खींचती है, और अचानक कहीं ज़्यादा तेज़ घूमने लगती है, जबकि किसी ने धक्का नहीं दिया।
Angular momentum, जिसे L लिखते हैं, rotation के लिए वही role निभाता है जो ordinary momentum p straight-line motion के लिए।

और linear momentum की तरह, यह बदलने का विरोध करता है। घूमता lattu सीधा खड़ा रहता है, चलती cycle खड़ी cycle से कहीं आसानी से balance होती है, और spun cricket ball अपनी line पकड़े रहती है, सब इसलिए कि angular momentum locked in है।

Dancer पर वापस। वह बाहें अंदर खींचती है, जिससे उसका moment of inertia घटता है। चूँकि angular momentum, यानी moment of inertia गुणा omega, external torque न होने पर constant रहना चाहिए, moment of inertia घटते ही omega को ऊपर उछलना पड़ता है। बाहें अंदर, spin तेज़।

यही law आसमान भी चलाता है। एक planet पर हमेशा Sun की ओर force होता है, जिसका Sun के बारे में torque zero है, तो उसका angular momentum conserved है। इसीलिए पास आने पर वह तेज़ और दूर जाने पर धीमा होता है, छुपा हुआ Kepler second law।

<excited> इसे और आगे ले जाओ तो physics की सबसे नाटकीय घटनाओं में से एक मिलती है। जब कोई विशाल star सिमटकर एक नन्हा neutron star बनता है, उसका moment of inertia गिर जाता है, और angular momentum बचाने के लिए उसकी spin rate फट पड़ती है; कुछ neutron stars एक second में सैकड़ों बार घूमते हैं।

एक चेतावनी जो exam questions तय करती है — यह conservation सिर्फ़ तब है जब net external torque zero हो। Internal forces, जैसे dancer की muscles, moment of inertia और omega को rearrange कर सकती हैं, पर total angular momentum को कभी नहीं बदल सकतीं।

board_events.text: Torque and energy share units, but torque is a vector in newton metres, never joules.

segments.text: Here is the complete toolkit for torque and angular momentum. Almost every problem in this subtopic is one of these lines.
The figure fixes the first one. Torque equals r times F times sine theta, which is the same as the moment arm, the perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of the force, times F.
So torque is the cross product r cross F, and its magnitude is r F sine theta, equal to the perpendicular distance times the force.

The master equation of rotational dynamics: the net torque equals the moment of inertia times angular acceleration, which also equals the rate of change of angular momentum. That is Newton second law in rotational language.
Angular momentum of a particle is r cross p, that is r cross m v; for a rigid body about a fixed axis it becomes the moment of inertia times omega.

The conservation law: when the net external torque is zero, angular momentum is constant, so the moment of inertia times omega before equals the same product after. This is the skater, the planets, and coupling wheels in one line.
Rotational kinetic energy is one half moment of inertia omega squared, which can also be written as L squared over two I. And rotational power is torque dotted with angular velocity.

<curious> One warning worth a mark: torque and energy come out with the same dimensions, but torque is a vector measured in newton metres, while energy is a scalar in joules. Never write torque in joules.
यह रहा torque और angular momentum का पूरा toolkit। इस subtopic का लगभग हर problem इन्हीं lines में से एक है।
Figure पहली को पक्का करती है। Torque बराबर r गुणा F गुणा sine theta, जो वही है — moment arm यानी axis से force की line तक perpendicular distance — गुणा F।
तो torque है cross product r cross F, और उसकी magnitude है r F sine theta, बराबर perpendicular distance गुणा force।

Rotational dynamics की master equation — net torque बराबर moment of inertia गुणा angular acceleration, जो angular momentum के change की rate के भी बराबर है। यह rotational भाषा में Newton का second law है।
किसी particle का angular momentum है r cross p, यानी r cross m v; fixed axis के बारे में rigid body के लिए यह moment of inertia गुणा omega बन जाता है।

Conservation law — जब net external torque zero हो, angular momentum constant है, तो पहले का moment of inertia गुणा omega बाद के उसी product के बराबर। यह skater, planets और coupling wheels, एक ही line में।
Rotational kinetic energy है one half moment of inertia omega square, जिसे L square बटा two I भी लिख सकते हैं। और rotational power है torque dot angular velocity।

<curious> एक चेतावनी जो एक mark की है — torque और energy की dimensions same निकलती हैं, पर torque एक vector है जो newton metres में मापा जाता है, जबकि energy एक scalar है joules में। Torque को कभी joules में मत लिखो।
