</svg>

board_events.text: Slice the sphere into thin discs along the axis; each slice at height $y$ has radius $r=\sqrt{R^2-y^2}$.
The slice uses the disc result: chaining disc into sphere.

segments.text: The J E E Advanced showpiece: derive the moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere about a diameter, by integration.
The strategy, shown in the figure, is to slice the sphere into thin discs stacked along the diameter, and integrate using the disc result.
Take a slice at height y from the centre. Its radius is the square root of R squared minus y squared, and it has a small thickness dee y.
The mass of the slice: with volume density rho, the slice volume is pi r squared dee y, so dee m is rho pi times R squared minus y squared, dee y.
The moment of the slice about the axis is the disc result, half the slice mass times r squared. That is half rho pi times R squared minus y squared, squared, dee y.
Integrate from minus R to plus R. Expanding and integrating the polynomial gives sixteen R to the fifth over fifteen, times one half rho pi.

Finally substitute the density rho, which is the mass over four thirds pi R cubed. The R powers and the constants tidy up, and the moment of inertia is two fifths M R squared, the standard result confirmed from first principles.
<excited> And notice the theme once more: the slice used the disc result. We chained the disc into the sphere, which is exactly the master technique of this subtopic in action.
J E E Advanced की showpiece — integration से एक uniform solid sphere का, एक diameter के बारे में moment of inertia derive करो।
Strategy, figure में दिखाई, है sphere को diameter के साथ stacked पतली discs में slice करना, और disc result से integrate करना।
Centre से height y पर एक slice लो। उसका radius है R square minus y square का square root, और उसकी छोटी thickness dee y है।
Slice की mass — volume density rho के साथ, slice का volume है pi r square dee y, तो dee m है rho pi गुणा R square minus y square, dee y।
Axis के बारे में slice का moment है disc result, आधा slice mass गुणा r square। यानी आधा rho pi गुणा R square minus y square, का square, dee y।
Minus R से plus R तक integrate करो। Polynomial को expand और integrate करने पर मिलता है sixteen R की fifth power बटा fifteen, गुणा आधा rho pi।

आख़िर में density rho substitute करो, जो mass बटा four thirds pi R cube है। R की powers और constants साफ़ हो जाते हैं, और moment of inertia है two fifths M R square, standard result first principles से confirmed।
<excited> और theme एक बार फिर देखो — slice ने disc result इस्तेमाल किया। हमने disc को sphere में chain किया, जो ठीक इस subtopic की master technique काम करते हुए है।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Moment-of-inertia traps
1. Using the wrong distance in $m r^2$; the $r$ is the perpendicular distance from the axis.
For a corner mass on a square about the centre, r is half the diagonal, not half the side.
2. Applying the perpendicular axis theorem to 3D bodies; it is for flat laminae only.
3. Mixing up standard formulas: disc-centre versus disc-diameter, solid sphere versus shell.
4. Thinking the radius of gyration moves with mass; K depends only on geometry and axis.
Pro-tip: for an off-centre axis, reach for the parallel axis theorem before integrating.
Most hard problems are one standard formula plus one theorem; spot the pair and the work collapses.

segments.text: Let us close moment of inertia with the four traps and the pro-tips that shrink most problems.
Trap one: using the wrong distance in mass times r squared. The r is the perpendicular distance from the axis, never the distance from the centre of mass or from a random point.
For a corner mass on a square rotating about the centre, r is half the diagonal, not half the side. That single confusion loses marks constantly.
Trap two: applying the perpendicular-axis theorem to three-dimensional bodies. It is for flat laminae only, so reaching for it on a sphere or a cylinder is an instant wrong answer.

Trap three: mixing up the standard formulas. Disc about the centre is half M R squared, but about a diameter it is a quarter M R squared; a solid sphere is two fifths M R squared, but a shell is two thirds. Build a clean mental table and rehearse it.
Trap four: thinking the radius of gyration moves with mass. K depends only on the geometry and the axis. Add or remove uniform mass and K can stay put, or even rise, as in a hollowed disc.

<whisper> And the pro-tips. For a moment about an off-centre axis, reach for the parallel-axis theorem before you integrate. And for any flat plate, the perpendicular-axis theorem turns one hard integral into two easy ones.
Most hard moment-of-inertia problems are really one standard formula plus one theorem. Spot that pair and the work collapses to a couple of lines.
Moment of inertia को उन चार traps और उन pro-tips के साथ बंद करते हैं जो ज़्यादातर problems को छोटा कर देते हैं।
Trap one — mass गुणा r square में ग़लत distance इस्तेमाल करना। r axis से perpendicular distance है, कभी centre of mass या किसी random point से distance नहीं।
Centre के बारे में घूमते square पर एक corner mass के लिए, r diagonal का आधा है, side का आधा नहीं। यही एक confusion लगातार marks गँवाता है।
Trap two — perpendicular-axis theorem को three-dimensional bodies पर लगाना। यह सिर्फ़ flat laminae के लिए है, तो sphere या cylinder पर इसे उठाना तुरंत ग़लत answer है।

Trap three — standard formulas को मिला देना। Disc centre के बारे में आधा M R square है, पर diameter के बारे में एक-चौथाई M R square; solid sphere two fifths M R square है, पर shell two thirds। एक साफ़ mental table बनाओ और उसे रटो।
Trap four — यह सोचना कि radius of gyration mass के साथ बदलता है। K सिर्फ़ geometry और axis पर निर्भर करता है। Uniform mass जोड़ो या हटाओ, K वैसा रह सकता है, या बढ़ भी सकता है, जैसे hollowed disc में।

<whisper> और pro-tips। Off-centre axis के बारे में moment के लिए, integrate करने से पहले parallel-axis theorem की ओर जाओ। और किसी भी flat plate के लिए, perpendicular-axis theorem एक कठिन integral को दो आसान में बदल देता है।
ज़्यादातर कठिन moment-of-inertia problems असल में एक standard formula plus एक theorem हैं। उस जोड़ी को पहचानो और काम दो-चार lines में सिमट जाता है।

board_events.text: Every quantity of linear motion has a rotational twin, measured in angle instead of distance.
Angular displacement theta replaces distance; angular velocity omega replaces speed.
Angular acceleration alpha is the rate of change of angular velocity, the twin of linear acceleration.
For a rigid body, every particle sweeps the same angle in the same time: one omega for the whole body.
So the three kinematic equations you know for constant a carry over, symbol for symbol.
This single analogy means you have already done most of the work for this subtopic.

segments.text: Here is the good news that opens this subtopic: rotational motion is not a new subject to learn from scratch. Every idea from straight-line kinematics has an exact rotational twin.

The figure names the three key quantities. As the wheel turns, it sweeps an angular displacement theta, it turns at an angular velocity omega, and if that spin rate changes, it has an angular acceleration alpha.
The correspondence is precise. Every quantity of linear motion has a rotational partner, measured in angle rather than distance.
Angular displacement theta replaces distance, and angular velocity omega, the rate of change of theta, replaces ordinary speed.
And angular acceleration alpha is the rate of change of angular velocity, the exact twin of linear acceleration. When omega grows, alpha is positive; when it shrinks, alpha is negative.
A crucial simplification for a rigid body: every particle in it sweeps the same angle in the same time. So the whole body shares one omega and one alpha, no matter how big it is.

Because of that, the three equations of motion you already know for constant linear acceleration carry straight over to rotation, symbol for symbol. Distance becomes angle, velocity becomes angular velocity, acceleration becomes angular acceleration.
<curious> This one analogy is a gift: it means you have already done most of the work for this subtopic. You are not learning new physics, you are re-labelling physics you own.
इस subtopic को खोलती अच्छी ख़बर — rotational motion कोई नया विषय नहीं जो scratch से सीखना पड़े। Straight-line kinematics का हर idea एक बिलकुल सटीक rotational twin रखता है।

Figure तीन key quantities के नाम बताती है। जैसे wheel घूमता है, वह एक angular displacement theta sweep करता है, angular velocity omega पर घूमता है, और अगर वह spin rate बदले, तो उसकी एक angular acceleration alpha है।
Correspondence सटीक है। Linear motion की हर quantity का एक rotational partner है, distance के बजाय angle में मापा गया।
Angular displacement theta, distance की जगह लेता है, और angular velocity omega, theta के change की rate, ordinary speed की जगह।
और angular acceleration alpha है angular velocity के change की rate, linear acceleration का बिलकुल twin। जब omega बढ़े, alpha positive; जब घटे, alpha negative।
एक rigid body के लिए अहम simplification — उसका हर particle एक ही समय में एक ही angle sweep करता है। तो पूरी body एक omega और एक alpha share करती है, चाहे कितनी भी बड़ी हो।

इसी वजह से, constant linear acceleration के लिए जो तीन equations of motion आप जानते हो, वे सीधे rotation पर आ जाती हैं, symbol दर symbol। Distance बनता है angle, velocity बनती है angular velocity, acceleration बनती है angular acceleration।
<curious> यह एक analogy एक तोहफ़ा है — इसका मतलब आप इस subtopic का ज़्यादातर काम पहले ही कर चुके हो। आप नई physics नहीं सीख रहे, आप अपनी ही physics को नया label दे रहे हो।

board_events.text: Rotational Newton second law: net torque equals moment of inertia times angular acceleration.
Torque replaces force; moment of inertia replaces mass; angular acceleration replaces acceleration.
A spinning body stores rotational kinetic energy, one half I omega squared.
A torque acting through an angle does work: $W = \tau\,\theta$, changing that energy.
The bridge to linear quantities for a point at radius $r$: $v = \omega r$ and $a = \alpha r$.
Learn the analogy table once, and every rotational law writes itself.

segments.text: With the kinematics mirrored, the dynamics mirror too. Force, mass, and energy all have rotational partners, and the figure lays the full dictionary out side by side.

Study this table for a moment; it is the master key to the whole subtopic. Position pairs with angle, velocity with angular velocity, mass with moment of inertia, force with torque, and so on down the list.

The centrepiece is the rotational form of Newton second law: the net torque on a body equals its moment of inertia times its angular acceleration. Compare it with force equals mass times acceleration and the pattern is unmistakable.
Read off the replacements. Torque plays the role of force, moment of inertia plays the role of mass, and angular acceleration plays the role of acceleration.
Energy transfers too. A spinning body stores rotational kinetic energy equal to one half the moment of inertia times omega squared, the exact twin of one half m v squared.

And a torque that acts through an angle does work: the work is the torque times the angle turned, and that work changes the rotational kinetic energy, just as force times distance does for linear motion.

Finally, the bridge that connects the two worlds. For any point at a distance r from the axis, its linear speed is omega times r, and its linear acceleration along the motion is alpha times r. This is how a spinning wheel becomes a moving car.
<excited> Learn this analogy table once and internalise it, and every rotational law writes itself. You never memorise them separately; you translate.
Kinematics के mirror होते ही dynamics भी mirror होती है। Force, mass, और energy, सबके rotational partners हैं, और figure पूरी dictionary साथ-साथ बिछा देती है।
इस table को एक पल देखिए; यह पूरे subtopic की master key है। Position की जोड़ी angle से, velocity की angular velocity से, mass की moment of inertia से, force की torque से, और list में नीचे तक ऐसे ही।

केंद्र में है Newton के second law का rotational रूप — किसी body पर net torque बराबर उसका moment of inertia गुणा उसकी angular acceleration। इसे force बराबर mass गुणा acceleration से मिलाओ और pattern साफ़ है।
Replacements पढ़ लो। Torque force का role निभाता है, moment of inertia mass का, और angular acceleration acceleration का।
Energy भी transfer होती है। एक spinning body rotational kinetic energy जमा करती है, बराबर one half moment of inertia गुणा omega square, one half m v square का बिलकुल twin।
और एक torque जो किसी angle से act करे, work करता है — work है torque गुणा घुमाया गया angle, और वह work rotational kinetic energy बदलता है, ठीक जैसे linear motion में force गुणा distance।

आख़िर में वह bridge जो दोनों दुनियाओं को जोड़ता है। Axis से distance r पर किसी भी point के लिए, उसकी linear speed है omega गुणा r, और motion के साथ linear acceleration है alpha गुणा r। इसी तरह एक घूमता wheel एक चलती car बन जाता है।
<excited> इस analogy table को एक बार सीख लो और आत्मसात कर लो, फिर हर rotational law खुद लिख जाता है। आप उन्हें अलग-अलग रटते नहीं; आप translate करते हो।

board_events.latex: v = \omega r,\qquad a_{tangential} = \alpha r,\qquad a_{centripetal} = \omega^2 r

board_events.text: The kinematic three hold only for constant angular acceleration.

segments.text: Here is the compact toolkit. Three kinematic equations, the dynamics, the energy, and the linear bridge.
The figure shows the bridge in action: a point at radius r on a spinning body moves at a linear speed omega times r, faster the farther out it sits.
First kinematic equation: the final angular velocity is the initial plus alpha times t. This is v equals u plus a t, translated.
Second: the angle turned is omega-naught t plus one half alpha t squared. That is s equals u t plus one half a t squared, translated.
Third: omega squared equals omega-naught squared plus two alpha theta. That is the timeless equation, v squared equals u squared plus two a s, translated.

Then the dynamics and energy in one line: net torque is the moment of inertia times alpha; rotational kinetic energy is one half the moment of inertia omega squared; work is torque times angle; and power is torque times omega.
And the linear bridge: linear speed is omega r, the tangential acceleration is alpha r, and the centripetal acceleration pulling toward the centre is omega squared r.
One condition to respect: those three kinematic equations hold only when the angular acceleration is constant, exactly as their linear cousins require constant a.
यह रहा compact toolkit। तीन kinematic equations, dynamics, energy, और linear bridge।
Figure bridge को काम करते दिखाती है — spinning body पर radius r के किसी point की linear speed है omega गुणा r, जितना बाहर उतना तेज़।
पहली kinematic equation — final angular velocity बराबर initial plus alpha गुणा t। यह है v बराबर u plus a t, translated।
दूसरी — घुमाया गया angle है omega-naught t plus one half alpha t square। यह है s बराबर u t plus one half a t square, translated।
तीसरी — omega square बराबर omega-naught square plus two alpha theta। यह वह timeless equation है, v square बराबर u square plus two a s, translated।

फिर dynamics और energy एक line में — net torque है moment of inertia गुणा alpha; rotational kinetic energy है one half moment of inertia omega square; work है torque गुणा angle; और power है torque गुणा omega।
और linear bridge — linear speed है omega r, tangential acceleration है alpha r, और centre की ओर खींचती centripetal acceleration है omega square r।
एक condition का ध्यान रखो — वे तीन kinematic equations सिर्फ़ तब चलती हैं जब angular acceleration constant हो, ठीक जैसे उनके linear cousins को constant a चाहिए।

board_events.text: Deriving the rotational equations of motion

board_events.text: Constant alpha means $\alpha = \tfrac{d\omega}{dt}$ is fixed; integrate once for omega.
The angle is the area under the omega-time line, a trapezium.
Work-energy for rotation: $W = \tau\theta = \tfrac12 I\omega^2 - \tfrac12 I\omega_0^2$.
Every step is the linear derivation with angular symbols swapped in.

segments.text: Let us derive the rotational equations of motion, then the work-energy theorem for rotation. Each derivation is the linear one you have already seen, wearing angular symbols.
The figure is the whole first proof in one picture: with constant alpha, the angular velocity rises as a straight line, and the area under it is the angle turned.
Start from constant angular acceleration, which means alpha, the rate of change of omega, is a fixed number. Integrate that once with respect to time.
Integrating gives the angular velocity as omega-naught plus alpha t, the first equation. It says the spin rate climbs steadily.
Now the angle turned is the area under the omega-versus-time line, which is a trapezium: a rectangle omega-naught t plus a triangle one half alpha t squared.

That gives theta equals omega-naught t plus one half alpha t squared, the second equation. Eliminate the time between the first two, and you get omega squared equals omega-naught squared plus two alpha theta, the third.

Now the work-energy theorem for rotation. The work done by a constant torque through an angle theta is torque times theta, and by the dynamics that equals the change in rotational kinetic energy, one half the moment of inertia omega squared minus one half the moment of inertia omega-naught squared.
<whisper> Look back and you will see it: every single step is the familiar linear derivation with angular symbols swapped in. Learn one, and you own both.
पहले rotational equations of motion derive करते हैं, फिर rotation के लिए work-energy theorem। हर derivation वही linear वाली है जो आप देख चुके हो, angular symbols पहने हुए।
Figure पूरा पहला proof एक तस्वीर में है — constant alpha के साथ, angular velocity एक सीधी line की तरह उठती है, और उसके नीचे का area घुमाया गया angle है।
Constant angular acceleration से शुरू करो, जिसका मतलब alpha, omega के change की rate, एक fixed number है। उसे time के respect में एक बार integrate करो।
Integrate करने पर angular velocity मिलती है omega-naught plus alpha t, पहली equation। यह कहती है spin rate लगातार चढ़ती है।
अब घुमाया गया angle है omega-बनाम-time line के नीचे का area, जो एक trapezium है — एक rectangle omega-naught t plus एक triangle one half alpha t square।
इससे मिलता है theta बराबर omega-naught t plus one half alpha t square, दूसरी equation। पहली दो के बीच से time हटाओ, तो मिलता है omega square बराबर omega-naught square plus two alpha theta, तीसरी।

अब rotation के लिए work-energy theorem। किसी constant torque का angle theta से किया work है torque गुणा theta, और dynamics से वह बराबर है rotational kinetic energy के change के, one half moment of inertia omega square minus one half moment of inertia omega-naught square।
<whisper> पीछे देखो और दिख जाएगा — हर एक step वही जाना-पहचाना linear derivation है, angular symbols के साथ। एक सीखो, दोनों के मालिक बनो।

board_events.text: A wheel starts from rest with constant $\alpha = 2$ rad per second squared for $t = 5$ s.
Convert to revolutions if asked: divide by two pi.
Start with omega naught equal to zero; pick the equation with only known symbols.

segments.text: A clean board-level kinematics problem. A wheel starts from rest and spins up with a constant angular acceleration of two radians per second squared. Find its angular velocity and the angle it turns through after five seconds.
The figure sets the scene: the wheel begins at rest and steadily builds up its spin under a constant alpha.
Write the givens: initial angular velocity zero, alpha two radians per second squared, and time five seconds.
For the angular velocity, use omega equals omega-naught plus alpha t. That is zero plus two times five, which is ten radians per second.
For the angle, use theta equals omega-naught t plus one half alpha t squared. The first term is zero, and the second is one half times two times twenty-five, which is twenty-five radians.
If the question asks for revolutions instead of radians, just divide by two pi, since one revolution is two pi radians.
So the number of revolutions is twenty-five over two pi, which is about three point nine eight revolutions, roughly four full turns.
The habit to build: write omega-naught equals zero explicitly, then pick the one equation that contains only symbols you already know.

एक साफ़ board-level kinematics problem। एक wheel rest से शुरू होता है और two radians per second square के constant angular acceleration से spin up करता है। पाँच seconds बाद उसकी angular velocity और घुमाया गया angle निकालो।
Figure दृश्य set करती है — wheel rest से शुरू होता है और constant alpha के तहत अपनी spin लगातार बढ़ाता है।
Givens लिखो — initial angular velocity zero, alpha two radians per second square, और time five seconds।
Angular velocity के लिए omega बराबर omega-naught plus alpha t use करो। यानी zero plus two गुणा five, जो ten radians per second।
Angle के लिए theta बराबर omega-naught t plus one half alpha t square use करो। पहला term zero है, और दूसरा one half गुणा two गुणा twenty-five, जो twenty-five radians।
अगर question radians के बजाय revolutions माँगे, तो बस two pi से भाग दो, क्योंकि one revolution है two pi radians।
तो revolutions की संख्या है twenty-five बटा two pi, जो लगभग three point nine eight revolutions, क़रीब चार पूरे चक्कर।
बनाने लायक़ आदत — omega-naught बराबर zero साफ़ लिखो, फिर वही एक equation चुनो जिसमें सिर्फ़ वे symbols हों जो पहले से पता हैं।

segments.text: A N E E T problem that ties the dynamics to the kinematics. A flywheel with a moment of inertia of zero point five kilogram metre squared is driven from rest by a constant torque of ten newton metres for four seconds. Find its final angular velocity.
The figure shows the flywheel, its mass at the rim, being spun up by the applied torque.
The trap is to reach straight for a kinematic equation and get stuck, because you are not given alpha. You must find alpha first from the dynamics, then feed it into the kinematics.
Write the givens: moment of inertia zero point five kilogram metre squared, torque ten newton metres, starting from rest, for four seconds.
Stage one, the dynamics. Newton second law for rotation gives alpha as the torque over the moment of inertia, which is ten over zero point five, that is twenty radians per second squared.
Stage two, the kinematics. Now omega is omega-naught plus alpha t, which is zero plus twenty times four, giving eighty radians per second.
So the whole path is two stages: the dynamics hands you alpha, then the kinematics hands you omega. Recognising that a problem needs both is the real skill.
A quick sanity check: a bigger torque or a smaller moment of inertia would each raise alpha, and therefore raise the final omega. The answer scales the way intuition expects.

एक N E E T problem जो dynamics को kinematics से जोड़ती है। zero point five kilogram metre square के moment of inertia वाला एक flywheel, rest से, ten newton metres के constant torque से चार seconds चलाया जाता है। उसकी final angular velocity निकालो।
Figure flywheel दिखाती है, उसकी mass rim पर, applied torque से spin up होते हुए।
Trap है सीधे किसी kinematic equation पर जाना और अटक जाना, क्योंकि alpha दिया नहीं है। पहले dynamics से alpha निकालो, फिर उसे kinematics में डालो।
Givens लिखो — moment of inertia zero point five kilogram metre square, torque ten newton metres, rest से शुरू, चार seconds के लिए।
Stage one, dynamics। Rotation के लिए Newton का second law देता है alpha बराबर torque बटा moment of inertia, जो ten बटा zero point five, यानी twenty radians per second square।
Stage two, kinematics। अब omega है omega-naught plus alpha t, जो zero plus twenty गुणा four, देता है eighty radians per second।
तो पूरा रास्ता दो stages है — dynamics आपको alpha देती है, फिर kinematics आपको omega। यह पहचानना कि problem को दोनों चाहिए, असली skill है।
एक झटपट sanity check — बड़ा torque या छोटा moment of inertia, दोनों alpha बढ़ाते, और इसलिए final omega। Answer वैसे ही scale करता है जैसे intuition उम्मीद करती है।

board_events.text: A disc at $\omega_0 = 20$ rad/s stops in $100$ revolutions; find the retardation and braking torque.
Use the timeless equation when time is absent but angle is given.

segments.text: A J E E Main problem using the timeless equation. A disc spinning at twenty radians per second is brought to rest in exactly one hundred revolutions by a steady braking torque. Find the angular retardation, and the torque if the moment of inertia is two kilogram metre squared.
The figure shows the braking torque opposing the spin, steadily slowing omega down to zero.
Write the givens carefully: initial angular velocity twenty radians per second, final angular velocity zero, and the angle is one hundred revolutions.
Convert the angle to radians: one hundred revolutions times two pi is two hundred pi radians. And the final omega is zero.
Time is not given, so use the timeless equation, omega squared equals omega-naught squared plus two alpha theta. That becomes zero equals four hundred plus two alpha times two hundred pi.

Solve for alpha. It is minus four hundred over four hundred pi, which is minus one over pi, about minus zero point three two radians per second squared. The minus sign correctly marks it as a retardation.
For the torque, take its magnitude as the moment of inertia times the magnitude of alpha. With a moment of inertia of two, the braking torque is two over pi, about zero point six four newton metres.
<curious> The lesson: whenever time is absent but the angle is given, the timeless equation is your shortcut. It skips finding the time entirely.

Timeless equation इस्तेमाल करती एक J E E Main problem। twenty radians per second पर घूमती एक disc, एक steady braking torque से ठीक one hundred revolutions में रुक जाती है। Angular retardation निकालो, और torque भी अगर moment of inertia two kilogram metre square हो।
Figure braking torque को spin का विरोध करते दिखाती है, omega को लगातार zero तक धीमा करते हुए।
Givens ध्यान से लिखो — initial angular velocity twenty radians per second, final angular velocity zero, और angle one hundred revolutions।
Angle को radians में बदलो — one hundred revolutions गुणा two pi है two hundred pi radians। और final omega zero।
Time दिया नहीं, तो timeless equation use करो, omega square बराबर omega-naught square plus two alpha theta। यह बनता है zero बराबर four hundred plus two alpha गुणा two hundred pi।
alpha के लिए हल करो। यह है minus four hundred बटा four hundred pi, जो minus one बटा pi, लगभग minus zero point three two radians per second square। Minus sign इसे सही से retardation marks करता है।
Torque के लिए उसकी magnitude लो, moment of inertia गुणा alpha की magnitude। moment of inertia two के साथ, braking torque है two बटा pi, लगभग zero point six four newton metres।
<curious> सबक़ — जब भी time न हो पर angle दिया हो, timeless equation आपका shortcut है। यह time निकालना पूरी तरह छोड़ देती है।

board_events.text: Block $m$ hangs from a light string over a pulley (disc, mass $M$, radius $R$); find $a$.

board_events.latex: \text{Block: } mg - T = ma,\qquad \text{Pulley: } TR = I\alpha = \left(\tfrac12 MR^2\right)\alpha

board_events.text: Non-slip constraint links them: $a = \alpha R$.

board_events.latex: T = \tfrac12 M a,\qquad mg - \tfrac12 M a = ma

board_events.text: Notice $a \lt g$: the pulley inertia holds the block back.

segments.text: The J E E Advanced favourite that couples a block to a rotating pulley. A block of mass m hangs from a light string wrapped over a pulley, which is a uniform disc of mass M and radius R. Find the acceleration of the block as it falls.
The figure shows the setup and the crucial fact: the string does not slip on the pulley, so the block acceleration and the pulley angular acceleration are locked together.
Two bodies mean two equations. Write Newton second law for the block, and the rotational second law for the pulley.

For the block, its weight minus the tension equals mass times acceleration. For the pulley, the tension acts at radius R, giving a torque T R that equals the moment of inertia, half M R squared, times alpha.
Now the key link: because the string does not slip, the block linear acceleration equals alpha times R. This constraint is what marries the two equations.
Substitute the constraint into the pulley equation. The R terms simplify, and the tension comes out as half M a. Put that into the block equation: m g minus half M a equals m a.
Solve for the acceleration. It is m g over the quantity m plus M over two, which tidies to two m g over two m plus M.

<curious> And read the result: the acceleration is less than g. The pulley own inertia has to be spun up too, so it holds the falling block back. Set M to zero and you recover free fall, exactly as it should.

J E E Advanced की पसंदीदा जो एक block को एक rotating pulley से जोड़ती है। Mass m का एक block एक light string से लटका है जो एक pulley पर लिपटी है, जो mass M और radius R की एक uniform disc है। गिरते block का acceleration निकालो।
Figure setup और अहम बात दिखाती है — string pulley पर slip नहीं करती, तो block का acceleration और pulley का angular acceleration आपस में बँधे हैं।
दो bodies मतलब दो equations। Block के लिए Newton का second law लिखो, और pulley के लिए rotational second law।
Block के लिए, उसका weight minus tension बराबर mass गुणा acceleration। Pulley के लिए, tension radius R पर act करता है, torque T R देते हुए जो बराबर है moment of inertia, आधा M R square, गुणा alpha।
अब key link — क्योंकि string slip नहीं करती, block का linear acceleration बराबर है alpha गुणा R। यही constraint दोनों equations को जोड़ता है।
Constraint को pulley equation में substitute करो। R terms simplify होते हैं, और tension निकलता है आधा M a। इसे block equation में डालो — m g minus आधा M a बराबर m a।
Acceleration के लिए हल करो। यह है m g बटा quantity m plus M बटा two, जो साफ़ होकर two m g बटा two m plus M।

<curious> और result पढ़ो — acceleration g से कम है। Pulley की अपनी inertia को भी spin up करना पड़ता है, तो वह गिरते block को पीछे खींचती है। M को zero रखो और free fall वापस मिल जाता है, ठीक जैसा होना चाहिए।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Rotational-motion traps
1. Mixing degrees and radians; the equations demand radians throughout.
Convert revolutions to radians with two pi before substituting.
2. Using the kinematic equations when alpha is not constant; then you must integrate.
3. Forgetting the two-stage structure: torque gives alpha, then kinematics gives omega or theta.
4. Confusing tangential $a = \alpha r$ with centripetal $a = \omega^2 r$; they are perpendicular.
Pro-tip: build the linear-rotational analogy table once; then translate rather than memorise.
Non-slip problems always add the bridge $a = \alpha R$ as the extra equation.

segments.text: Let us close rotational motion with four traps and the pro-tip that unifies the whole subtopic.
Trap one: mixing degrees and radians. Every rotational equation of motion assumes radians throughout, so a stray degree quietly wrecks the answer.
In particular, convert revolutions to radians by multiplying by two pi before you substitute. Most silent errors here come from skipping that step.
Trap two: using the three kinematic equations when the angular acceleration is not constant. They are valid only for constant alpha; if the torque varies, you must go back to calculus and integrate.
Trap three: forgetting the two-stage structure of a dynamics problem. First the torque gives you alpha through Newton second law, and only then do the kinematics give you omega or theta.

Trap four: confusing the two accelerations of a point on a rotating body. The tangential acceleration alpha r speeds it up along its path, while the centripetal acceleration omega squared r pulls it toward the centre. They are perpendicular and must never be added as plain numbers.

<whisper> And the pro-tip that ties this subtopic together: build the linear-to-rotational analogy table once, thoroughly, and then translate every result rather than memorising a second set of formulas.
And remember the signature of a non-slip problem: the bridge a equals alpha R is always the extra equation that couples the linear and rotational parts. Spot it, and the system closes.
Rotational motion को चार traps और उस pro-tip के साथ बंद करते हैं जो पूरे subtopic को एक कर देता है।
Trap one — degrees और radians मिलाना। हर rotational equation of motion पूरे में radians मानती है, तो एक भटका हुआ degree चुपचाप answer बिगाड़ देता है।
ख़ासकर, substitute करने से पहले revolutions को two pi से गुणा करके radians में बदलो। यहाँ की ज़्यादातर silent errors उसी step को छोड़ने से आती हैं।
Trap two — तीन kinematic equations को तब इस्तेमाल करना जब angular acceleration constant न हो। वे सिर्फ़ constant alpha के लिए valid हैं; अगर torque बदले, तो calculus पर वापस जाकर integrate करना होगा।
Trap three — dynamics problem की two-stage संरचना भूल जाना। पहले torque Newton के second law से alpha देता है, और तभी kinematics आपको omega या theta देती है।

Trap four — rotating body पर किसी point के दो accelerations को confuse करना। Tangential acceleration alpha r उसे उसके path के साथ तेज़ करती है, जबकि centripetal acceleration omega square r उसे centre की ओर खींचती है। वे perpendicular हैं और कभी सादे numbers की तरह जोड़ी नहीं जानी चाहिए।
<whisper> और वह pro-tip जो इस subtopic को जोड़ता है — linear-से-rotational analogy table एक बार, अच्छी तरह बनाओ, फिर हर result translate करो, formulas का दूसरा set रटने के बजाय।
और non-slip problem की पहचान याद रखो — bridge a बराबर alpha R हमेशा वह extra equation है जो linear और rotational हिस्सों को जोड़ता है। उसे पहचानो, और system बंद हो जाता है।

board_events.text: A rolling wheel does two things together: its centre moves forward, and it spins.
Rolling without slipping locks them: $v_{cm} = \omega R$.
The contact point is momentarily at rest; that is why rolling friction is so gentle.
The bottom is at rest, the centre moves at v, and the top races at twice v.
The contact point acts as an instantaneous axis about which the whole wheel rotates.
Break the lock and it slips: spinning tyres on ice, or a skidding wheel.

segments.text: Rolling is the natural finale of this chapter, because it is translation and rotation happening together, the two motions we have studied all along, now fused.
The figure captures the surprising velocity picture. As the wheel rolls, its bottom point is momentarily still, its centre moves at speed v, and its top races along at twice that speed.
A rolling wheel is doing two things at once: its centre of mass glides forward in a straight line, and the wheel spins about that centre.

When it rolls without slipping, those two motions are locked together by one clean condition: the speed of the centre equals omega times the radius. Spin faster and you move faster, in exact proportion.
Here is the beautiful consequence. At each instant, the point touching the ground is momentarily at rest. It is not sliding, which is why rolling friction is so gentle compared with dragging.
So across the wheel, the velocities stack up: the bottom is at rest, the centre moves at v, and the top, adding the spin to the translation, races along at two v.
You can even picture the contact point as an instantaneous axis: at that frozen moment, the whole wheel is purely rotating about the point where it touches the ground.

<curious> Break the lock between spin and speed and the wheel slips instead of rolling. That is a tyre spinning uselessly on ice, or a braked wheel skidding. Rolling is the special, efficient case where the two stay perfectly matched.
Rolling इस chapter का स्वाभाविक finale है, क्योंकि यह translation और rotation एक साथ हैं, वही दो motions जो हम शुरू से पढ़ते आए, अब जुड़ी हुई।
Figure हैरान करने वाली velocity तस्वीर पकड़ती है। जैसे wheel roll करता है, उसका bottom point पल भर के लिए स्थिर है, centre speed v पर चलता है, और top उससे दुगनी speed पर दौड़ता है।
एक rolling wheel एक साथ दो काम कर रहा है — उसका centre of mass सीधी line में आगे सरकता है, और wheel उस centre के बारे में spin करता है।
जब वह बिना slip किए roll करता है, ये दोनों motions एक साफ़ condition से बँध जाती हैं — centre की speed बराबर omega गुणा radius। तेज़ spin करो तो तेज़ चलो, बिलकुल proportion में।
यहाँ सुंदर नतीजा है। हर पल, ज़मीन को छूता point पल भर के लिए स्थिर है। वह slide नहीं कर रहा, इसीलिए rolling friction, घसीटने के मुक़ाबले, इतनी हलकी है।
तो पूरे wheel में velocities जमती हैं — bottom स्थिर, centre v पर, और top, spin को translation में जोड़ते हुए, two v पर दौड़ता।
आप contact point को एक instantaneous axis भी मान सकते हो — उस जमे पल पर, पूरा wheel सिर्फ़ उस point के बारे में rotate कर रहा है जहाँ वह ज़मीन छूता है।

<curious> Spin और speed के बीच की lock तोड़ो और wheel roll के बजाय slip करता है। यह बर्फ़ पर बेकार घूमता tyre है, या braked wheel skid करता। Rolling वह ख़ास, efficient case है जहाँ दोनों बिलकुल मेल खाते रहते हैं।

board_events.text: A rolling body carries two kinds of kinetic energy at once.
Translational $\tfrac12 M v^2$ plus rotational $\tfrac12 I\omega^2$.
Using $v = \omega R$, the total is $\tfrac12 M v^2\left(1 + \tfrac{K^2}{R^2}\right)$.
So a rolling body always has more kinetic energy than a sliding one at the same speed.
Static friction supplies the torque that makes it roll, yet does no net work.
No friction, no rolling: on a frictionless slope a ball would only slide.

segments.text: Because rolling is two motions at once, its energy comes in two parts, and understanding that split unlocks every rolling problem.
The figure shows the two pieces side by side: the energy of moving forward and the energy of spinning.
A rolling body carries two kinds of kinetic energy at the same time, and both must be counted.
The translational part is one half M v squared, from the centre moving forward. The rotational part is one half the moment of inertia times omega squared, from the spin.

Using the rolling condition v equals omega R, the two combine neatly into one half M v squared times the bracket one plus K squared over R squared, where K is the radius of gyration. That bracket depends only on the shape.
One immediate consequence: a rolling body always has more kinetic energy than a body merely sliding at the same speed, because it must also account for the spin.

Now the subtle role of friction. It is static friction at the contact point that supplies the torque needed to spin the body up as it advances, yet because the contact point does not slide, that friction does no net work and drains no energy.

<excited> And the punchline: no friction, no rolling. On a perfectly frictionless slope, a ball has nothing to grip, so it would simply slide down without ever rotating. Friction is not the enemy of rolling; it is the very thing that makes rolling possible.
क्योंकि rolling एक साथ दो motions है, उसकी energy दो हिस्सों में आती है, और उस split को समझना हर rolling problem खोल देता है।
Figure दोनों टुकड़े साथ-साथ दिखाती है — आगे चलने की energy और spin करने की energy।
एक rolling body एक साथ दो तरह की kinetic energy रखती है, और दोनों गिननी हैं।
Translational हिस्सा है one half M v square, centre के आगे चलने से। Rotational हिस्सा है one half moment of inertia गुणा omega square, spin से।

Rolling condition v बराबर omega R से, दोनों साफ़-सुथरे जुड़ते हैं one half M v square गुणा bracket one plus K square बटा R square में, जहाँ K radius of gyration है। वह bracket सिर्फ़ shape पर निर्भर करता है।
एक तुरंत नतीजा — एक rolling body की kinetic energy हमेशा उसी speed पर सिर्फ़ slide करती body से ज़्यादा होती है, क्योंकि उसे spin भी गिननी है।

अब friction का सूक्ष्म role। यह contact point पर static friction है जो body को आगे बढ़ते हुए spin up करने का torque देती है, फिर भी क्योंकि contact point slide नहीं करता, वह friction कोई net work नहीं करती और energy नहीं निकालती।

<excited> और punchline — no friction, no rolling। एक बिलकुल frictionless slope पर, गेंद के पास पकड़ने को कुछ नहीं, तो वह बिना कभी rotate किए बस नीचे slide कर जाती। Friction rolling की दुश्मन नहीं; यही वह चीज़ है जो rolling को मुमकिन बनाती है।

board_events.text: Smaller I over M R squared means larger acceleration: the sphere wins the race.

segments.text: Here is the rolling toolkit, and almost every rolling question is one of these lines.
The figure previews the headline result: the acceleration of a body rolling down an incline, softened by a bracket that depends on its shape.
First the rolling conditions: the centre speed is omega R, and differentiating, the centre acceleration is alpha R.

The total kinetic energy is one half M v squared plus one half the moment of inertia omega squared, which collapses using the rolling condition to one half M v squared times one plus K squared over R squared.

The star formula: a body rolling down an incline of angle theta accelerates at g sine theta divided by one plus the moment of inertia over M R squared. That denominator is always bigger than one, so a rolling body accelerates slower than a frictionless sliding block.
By energy conservation, the speed at the bottom after descending a height h is the square root of two g h over one plus K squared over R squared. Notice the mass has cancelled: it does not matter.
The shape factor, the moment of inertia over M R squared, takes clean values: one for a ring, one half for a disc, and two fifths for a solid sphere.
<curious> And the single rule that decides every rolling race: the smaller the shape factor, the larger the acceleration. That is why the solid sphere, with the smallest factor, always wins.
यह रहा rolling toolkit, और लगभग हर rolling सवाल इन्हीं lines में से एक है।
Figure headline result की झलक देती है — किसी incline से नीचे roll करती body का acceleration, एक bracket से नरम, जो उसके shape पर निर्भर करता है।
पहले rolling conditions — centre की speed है omega R, और differentiate करने पर centre का acceleration है alpha R।
Total kinetic energy है one half M v square plus one half moment of inertia omega square, जो rolling condition से सिमटकर one half M v square गुणा one plus K square बटा R square।

Star formula — angle theta के incline से नीचे roll करती body g sine theta बटा one plus moment of inertia बटा M R square पर accelerate करती है। वह denominator हमेशा one से बड़ा है, तो rolling body एक frictionless sliding block से धीमा accelerate करती है।
Energy conservation से, height h उतरने के बाद bottom पर speed है two g h बटा one plus K square बटा R square का square root। ध्यान दो mass cancel हो गई — उसका कोई मतलब नहीं।
Shape factor, moment of inertia बटा M R square, साफ़ values लेता है — ring के लिए one, disc के लिए one half, और solid sphere के लिए two fifths।
<curious> और वह एक rule जो हर rolling race तय करता है — shape factor जितना छोटा, acceleration उतना बड़ा। इसीलिए solid sphere, सबसे छोटे factor के साथ, हमेशा जीतता है।

board_events.text: Rolling energy and the incline acceleration

board_events.caption: M g h at the top becomes moving plus spinning at the bottom

board_events.text: Energy method for the incline: all the height energy becomes rolling kinetic energy.
Force method gives the acceleration $a = \dfrac{g\sin\theta}{1 + I/MR^2}$; both agree.
The mass cancels, so the race depends only on the shape, never the size.

segments.text: Two derivations that power all of rolling: the energy split, and the acceleration down an incline. We will do the energy route in full, then quote the force route it matches.
The figure shows the energy bookkeeping: the height energy M g h at the top turns entirely into the two kinetic energies at the bottom.
Start with the total kinetic energy, one half M v squared plus one half the moment of inertia omega squared, and bring in the rolling condition, omega equals v over R.

Substitute and factor. The rotational term becomes one half M v squared times the moment of inertia over M R squared, so the whole kinetic energy is one half M v squared times one plus that shape factor.
Now the incline by energy. As the body rolls down a height h without slipping, friction does no net work, so all the gravitational potential energy becomes rolling kinetic energy.
Set M g h equal to one half M v squared times one plus K squared over R squared. Solve, and the mass cancels immediately, leaving the speed at the bottom set purely by the height and the shape.

If instead you use forces and torques, writing Newton second law along the slope together with torque equals I alpha, you get the acceleration as g sine theta over one plus the moment of inertia over M R squared. The two methods agree perfectly.
<excited> And the deep result both reveal: the mass cancels out. A rolling race down a ramp depends only on the shape, never on the size or the mass. A marble and a boulder of the same shape tie.
दो derivations जो पूरे rolling को चलाती हैं — energy split, और incline से नीचे acceleration। हम energy रास्ता पूरा करेंगे, फिर उससे मेल खाता force रास्ता quote करेंगे।
Figure energy का हिसाब दिखाती है — top पर height energy M g h पूरी तरह bottom पर दो kinetic energies में बदल जाती है।
Total kinetic energy से शुरू करो, one half M v square plus one half moment of inertia omega square, और rolling condition लाओ, omega बराबर v बटा R।
Substitute और factor करो। Rotational term बनता है one half M v square गुणा moment of inertia बटा M R square, तो पूरी kinetic energy है one half M v square गुणा one plus वह shape factor।
अब incline energy से। जैसे body बिना slip किए height h नीचे roll करती है, friction कोई net work नहीं करती, तो सारी gravitational potential energy rolling kinetic energy बन जाती है।
M g h को one half M v square गुणा one plus K square बटा R square के बराबर रखो। हल करो, और mass तुरंत cancel हो जाती है, bottom पर speed सिर्फ़ height और shape से तय होती है।

अगर इसके बजाय आप forces और torques इस्तेमाल करो, slope के साथ Newton का second law और torque बराबर I alpha लिखते हुए, तो acceleration मिलता है g sine theta बटा one plus moment of inertia बटा M R square। दोनों methods बिलकुल मेल खाते हैं।

<excited> और गहरा result जो दोनों दिखाते हैं — mass cancel हो जाती है। किसी ramp से नीचे rolling race सिर्फ़ shape पर निर्भर है, कभी size या mass पर नहीं। एक ही shape के एक marble और एक boulder बराबरी पर आते हैं।

board_events.text: The rotational share is $\dfrac{K^2/R^2}{1 + K^2/R^2}$; find it for a disc.
So one third of a rolling disc energy is rotational, two thirds translational.
For a ring the fraction is one half; for a solid sphere, two sevenths.
More mass at the rim locks a larger share of energy into spinning.

segments.text: A board favourite testing the energy split. What fraction of the total kinetic energy of a rolling disc is rotational?
The figure gives the answers for the three standard shapes; we will derive the disc case and read off the others.
The rotational fraction is the shape factor K squared over R squared, divided by one plus that same shape factor. For a disc the shape factor is one half.
Substitute one half. The fraction is one half over one plus one half.
That is one half over three halves, which is one third.
So exactly one third of a rolling disc kinetic energy lives in the spin, and the other two thirds is in the forward motion.
Run the same formula for the others: a ring, with shape factor one, gives one half; a solid sphere, with two fifths, gives two sevenths.
And the pattern is clear: the more mass a body keeps at its rim, the larger the share of its energy locked into spinning rather than moving.
Energy split test करती एक board favourite। एक rolling disc की total kinetic energy का कितना अंश rotational है?
Figure तीन standard shapes के answers देती है; हम disc case derive करेंगे और बाक़ी पढ़ लेंगे।
Rotational fraction है shape factor K square बटा R square, बटा one plus वही shape factor। Disc के लिए shape factor है one half।
One half substitute करो। Fraction है one half बटा one plus one half।
यानी one half बटा three halves, जो one third।
तो एक rolling disc की kinetic energy का ठीक one third spin में बसता है, और बाक़ी two thirds आगे की motion में।
बाक़ियों के लिए वही formula चलाओ — एक ring, shape factor one के साथ, देता है one half; एक solid sphere, two fifths के साथ, देता है two sevenths।
और pattern साफ़ है — body अपने rim पर जितनी ज़्यादा mass रखे, उसकी energy का उतना बड़ा अंश चलने के बजाय spin में बँध जाता है।

board_events.text: Trap: mass and radius do not matter; only the shape factor I over M R squared decides.
Acceleration $a = \dfrac{g\sin\theta}{1 + I/MR^2}$; smaller factor means faster.
Smaller shape factor gives larger acceleration, so the order of finish reverses it.
Solid sphere first, then disc, then ring, regardless of mass or size.

segments.text: The classic N E E T conceptual trap. A ring, a disc, and a solid sphere are released together from the top of the same incline. In what order do they reach the bottom?
The figure gives away the ending: the sphere leads, the disc follows, and the ring trails.

The trap is to think the heaviest or the largest wins. Neither mass nor radius appears in the acceleration, because they cancel. Only the shape factor, the moment of inertia over M R squared, decides.
The acceleration is g sine theta over one plus that shape factor. So the smaller the shape factor, the larger the acceleration, and the sooner it finishes.
Rank the factors: the ring is one, the disc is one half, and the sphere is two fifths. The ring has the largest, the sphere the smallest.
Because a smaller factor means a larger acceleration, the order of finishing reverses that ranking.
Put in numbers: the sphere accelerates at five sevenths g sine theta, the disc at two thirds, and the ring at one half. The sphere is clearly quickest.
<chuckle> So the solid sphere reaches the bottom first, then the disc, then the ring, every single time, no matter their masses or radii. Concentrate mass near the axis and you win the race.
Classic N E E T conceptual trap। एक ring, एक disc, और एक solid sphere एक ही incline के top से साथ छोड़े जाते हैं। वे किस क्रम में नीचे पहुँचते हैं?
Figure अंत बता देती है — sphere आगे, disc पीछे, और ring सबसे पीछे।
Trap है यह सोचना कि सबसे भारी या सबसे बड़ा जीतता है। न mass, न radius acceleration में आते हैं, क्योंकि वे cancel हो जाते हैं। सिर्फ़ shape factor, moment of inertia बटा M R square, तय करता है।
Acceleration है g sine theta बटा one plus वह shape factor। तो shape factor जितना छोटा, acceleration उतना बड़ा, और उतना जल्दी finish।
Factors को rank करो — ring one है, disc one half, और sphere two fifths। Ring सबसे बड़ा, sphere सबसे छोटा।
क्योंकि छोटा factor मतलब बड़ा acceleration, finishing का क्रम उस ranking को उलट देता है।
Numbers रखो — sphere five sevenths g sine theta पर accelerate करता है, disc two thirds पर, और ring one half पर। Sphere साफ़ तौर पर सबसे तेज़।
<chuckle> तो solid sphere सबसे पहले नीचे पहुँचता है, फिर disc, फिर ring, हर बार, चाहे उनकी mass या radii कुछ भी हों। Mass को axis के पास समेटो और race जीतो।

board_events.text: Solid sphere, $I = \tfrac25 MR^2$, on a $30^\circ$ incline; take $g = 10$ m per second squared.
Compare: a frictionless block would slide at $g\sin\theta = 5$ m per second squared.
The rolling sphere is slower because part of the drive goes into spinning it up.
Answer: about 3.57 metres per second squared down the slope.

segments.text: A J E E Main numerical, straight from the incline formula. A solid sphere rolls without slipping down a thirty-degree incline. Find its acceleration, taking g as ten metres per second squared.
The figure fixes the geometry: a solid sphere on a slope inclined at thirty degrees, with its shape factor of two fifths.
Write the givens: the sphere shape factor, the moment of inertia over M R squared, is two fifths, the angle is thirty degrees, and g is ten.
Substitute into the acceleration formula. The denominator is one plus two fifths, which is seven fifths, so the acceleration is five sevenths of g sine theta.
Now the numbers. Sine thirty is one half, so it is five sevenths times ten times one half, which is twenty-five over seven, about three point five seven metres per second squared.
Put it in context. A frictionless block on the same slope would slide at the full g sine theta, that is five metres per second squared.
The rolling sphere is noticeably slower, and the reason is physical: part of the gravitational drive is diverted into spinning the sphere up, leaving less for forward acceleration.
So the sphere rolls down at about three point five seven metres per second squared, comfortably less than the sliding value.
Incline formula से सीधा एक J E E Main numerical। एक solid sphere एक thirty-degree incline से बिना slip किए roll करता है। g को ten metres per second square लेते हुए उसका acceleration निकालो।
Figure geometry तय करती है — thirty degrees पर झुके slope पर एक solid sphere, अपने two fifths के shape factor के साथ।
Givens लिखो — sphere का shape factor, moment of inertia बटा M R square, two fifths है, angle thirty degrees, और g ten।
Acceleration formula में substitute करो। Denominator है one plus two fifths, जो seven fifths, तो acceleration है g sine theta का five sevenths।
अब numbers। Sine thirty है one half, तो यह five sevenths गुणा ten गुणा one half, जो twenty-five बटा seven, लगभग three point five seven metres per second square।
इसे context में रखो। उसी slope पर एक frictionless block पूरे g sine theta पर slide करता, यानी five metres per second square।
Rolling sphere साफ़ तौर पर धीमा है, और वजह physical है — gravitational drive का एक हिस्सा sphere को spin up करने में मुड़ जाता है, forward acceleration के लिए कम छोड़ते हुए।
तो sphere लगभग three point five seven metres per second square पर नीचे roll करता है, sliding value से आराम से कम।

board_events.text: For a body rolling down an incline, find the friction and the minimum coefficient needed.
No slipping requires $f \le \mu N = \mu Mg\cos\theta$.
Steeper slopes need more friction; beyond it, the sphere slips instead of rolling.

segments.text: The J E E Advanced capstone, digging into the friction itself. For a solid sphere rolling down an incline, find the friction force, and then the minimum coefficient of friction that keeps it rolling without slipping.
The figure shows friction acting up the slope. It is this friction that provides the torque to spin the sphere as it descends.
Set up the two equations, force along the slope and torque about the centre, and eliminate the acceleration between them to solve for the friction.

The friction comes out as M g sine theta divided by one plus M R squared over the moment of inertia, which you can also write with the shape factor as the fraction K squared over R squared, over one plus K squared over R squared, times M g sine theta.
For a solid sphere, with shape factor two fifths, that friction works out to two sevenths M g sine theta.
Now the condition for no slipping. The static friction available is at most mu times the normal force, and the normal force on the incline is M g cosine theta.
So set the required friction equal to mu times M g cosine theta and solve. The minimum coefficient of friction is two sevenths tangent theta.
<curious> And the physics is intuitive: steeper slopes have a larger tangent theta and so demand more friction. Tilt the ramp past that limit and even a sphere gives up rolling and begins to slip.

J E E Advanced की capstone, friction में ही गहराई से। एक incline से नीचे roll करते solid sphere के लिए friction force निकालो, फिर वह न्यूनतम coefficient of friction जो उसे बिना slip किए roll करते रखे।
Figure friction को slope के ऊपर की ओर act करते दिखाती है। यही friction वह torque देती है जो sphere को उतरते हुए spin कराती है।
दो equations set करो, slope के साथ force और centre के बारे में torque, और उनके बीच से acceleration हटाकर friction के लिए हल करो।

Friction निकलता है M g sine theta बटा one plus M R square बटा moment of inertia, जिसे आप shape factor के साथ भी लिख सकते हो, fraction K square बटा R square, बटा one plus K square बटा R square, गुणा M g sine theta।
एक solid sphere के लिए, two fifths के shape factor के साथ, वह friction बनता है two sevenths M g sine theta।
अब no slipping की condition। उपलब्ध static friction ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा mu गुणा normal force है, और incline पर normal force है M g cosine theta।
तो ज़रूरी friction को mu गुणा M g cosine theta के बराबर रखो और हल करो। न्यूनतम coefficient of friction है two sevenths tangent theta।
<curious> और physics सहज है — steeper slopes का tangent theta बड़ा होता है, तो ज़्यादा friction माँगते हैं। Ramp को उस हद से आगे झुकाओ और एक sphere भी rolling छोड़कर slip करने लगता है।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Rolling traps that cost marks
1. Counting only translational energy; a rolling body also stores $\tfrac12 I\omega^2$.
Always use the bracket $1 + K^2/R^2$ for rolling energy and speed.
2. Forgetting $v = \omega R$; without it the two motions are not linked.
3. Thinking heavier or bigger wins the race; mass and radius cancel out.
4. Believing friction does work here; static friction at the contact point does none.
Pro-tip: for a body released from a height, energy conservation is faster than forces.
Memorise the three shape factors, ring one, disc one half, sphere two fifths, and most rolling problems fall in seconds.

segments.text: Let us close rolling, and the chapter proper, with the four traps and the pro-tips that make rolling problems quick.

Trap one: counting only the translational energy. A rolling body also stores rotational kinetic energy, one half the moment of inertia omega squared, and dropping it under-counts the energy every time.
So always carry the bracket one plus K squared over R squared when you write the rolling energy or the speed at the bottom. That bracket is the whole difference between rolling and sliding.
Trap two: forgetting the rolling condition, v equals omega R. Without it, the translational and rotational parts float free and the problem will not close.
Trap three: thinking the heaviest or the biggest body wins the race down a ramp. Both the mass and the radius cancel, so only the shape decides.

Trap four: believing friction does work in pure rolling. Because the contact point is momentarily at rest, the static friction there does no net work, so mechanical energy is conserved even though friction is present.

<whisper> And the pro-tips. When a body is released from a height and you want its speed, energy conservation is almost always faster than forces and torques. And keep the three shape factors on instant recall.
Ring one, disc one half, solid sphere two fifths. With those three numbers memorised, most rolling problems, whether energy, acceleration, or a race, fall in seconds.
Rolling को, और असली chapter को, उन चार traps और उन pro-tips के साथ बंद करते हैं जो rolling problems को तेज़ बनाते हैं।
Trap one — सिर्फ़ translational energy गिनना। एक rolling body rotational kinetic energy भी जमा करती है, one half moment of inertia omega square, और उसे छोड़ना हर बार energy कम गिन देता है।
तो rolling energy या bottom पर speed लिखते समय हमेशा bracket one plus K square बटा R square रखो। वही bracket rolling और sliding के बीच का पूरा फ़र्क़ है।
Trap two — rolling condition भूल जाना, v बराबर omega R। उसके बिना translational और rotational हिस्से अलग तैरते रहते हैं और problem बंद नहीं होती।
Trap three — यह सोचना कि ramp से नीचे race में सबसे भारी या सबसे बड़ी body जीतती है। Mass और radius दोनों cancel हो जाते हैं, तो सिर्फ़ shape तय करता है।

Trap four — यह मानना कि pure rolling में friction work करती है। क्योंकि contact point पल भर के लिए स्थिर है, वहाँ की static friction कोई net work नहीं करती, तो friction होते हुए भी mechanical energy conserved रहती है।
<whisper> और pro-tips। जब कोई body किसी height से छोड़ी जाए और आपको उसकी speed चाहिए, energy conservation लगभग हमेशा forces और torques से तेज़ है। और तीन shape factors instant recall में रखो।
Ring one, disc one half, solid sphere two fifths। उन तीन numbers के रटे होने पर, ज़्यादातर rolling problems, चाहे energy, acceleration, या race, seconds में गिर जाते हैं।

sections.title: Chapter formula recap

board_events.text: Chapter formula recap

board_events.latex: \vec r_{cm} = \frac{\sum m_i \vec r_i}{M},\qquad M\vec a_{cm} = \vec F_{ext}
\vec A\times\vec B = AB\sin\theta\,\hat n,\qquad |\vec A\times\vec B| = AB\sin\theta
\vec L = \vec r\times\vec p,\quad L = I\omega,\quad \tau_{ext}=0 \Rightarrow L=\text{const}
I = \sum m_i r_i^2,\quad I = I_{cm} + Md^2,\quad I_z = I_x + I_y
K_{rot}=\tfrac12 I\omega^2,\qquad v=\omega r,\qquad a=\alpha r

segments.text: Here is the whole chapter distilled into its essential formulas, subtopic by subtopic. Treat this as your final revision pass.
Centre of mass: the mass-weighted average position, and the theorem that the external force equals the total mass times the acceleration of the centre of mass.
The vector product: magnitude A B sine theta along the perpendicular unit vector, and its size alone is A B sine theta.
Torque and its master law: torque is r cross F, and the net torque equals the moment of inertia times angular acceleration, which equals the rate of change of angular momentum.
Angular momentum: r cross p for a particle, the moment of inertia times omega for a rigid body, and conserved whenever the external torque is zero.
Equilibrium: the net force zero, the net torque zero, and for a lever, the principle of moments, force one times distance one equals force two times distance two.
Moment of inertia: the sum of m r squared, the parallel-axis theorem adding M d squared, and the perpendicular-axis theorem for flat laminae.
The three rotational equations of motion, exact mirrors of the linear ones, valid for constant angular acceleration.
Rotational kinetic energy is one half the moment of inertia omega squared, and the linear bridge gives v equals omega r and a equals alpha r.

And rolling: the centre speed is omega R, the incline acceleration carries the shape factor in its denominator, and the kinetic energy gains the bracket one plus K squared over R squared. That is the chapter, on one page.
यह रहा पूरा chapter अपने ज़रूरी formulas में सिमटा, subtopic दर subtopic। इसे अपना final revision pass समझो।
Centre of mass — mass-weighted average position, और वह theorem कि external force बराबर total mass गुणा centre of mass का acceleration।
Vector product — magnitude A B sine theta, perpendicular unit vector के साथ, और अकेली size है A B sine theta।
Torque और उसका master law — torque है r cross F, और net torque बराबर moment of inertia गुणा angular acceleration, जो angular momentum के change की rate के बराबर है।
Angular momentum — particle के लिए r cross p, rigid body के लिए moment of inertia गुणा omega, और conserved जब भी external torque zero हो।
Equilibrium — net force zero, net torque zero, और एक lever के लिए principle of moments, force one गुणा distance one बराबर force two गुणा distance two।
Moment of inertia — m r square का sum, parallel-axis theorem M d square जोड़ते हुए, और perpendicular-axis theorem flat laminae के लिए।
तीन rotational equations of motion, linear वालों के बिलकुल mirror, constant angular acceleration के लिए valid।
Rotational kinetic energy है one half moment of inertia omega square, और linear bridge देता है v बराबर omega r और a बराबर alpha r।

और rolling — centre की speed है omega R, incline acceleration अपने denominator में shape factor रखता है, और kinetic energy को bracket one plus K square बटा R square मिलता है। यही है पूरा chapter, एक page पर।

sections.title: Chapter cheat sheet

board_events.text: Chapter cheat sheet
Centre of mass moves as if all mass and all external force act there; internal forces never move it.
Cross product: right-hand rule for direction; use the determinant, mind the minus on the j term.
Torque turns, and net torque equals rate of change of angular momentum; conserve L when torque is zero.
Equilibrium needs BOTH: net force zero and net torque zero. Take torques about an unknown to remove it.
Standard I: ring M R squared, disc half M R squared, solid sphere two fifths M R squared, rod-centre M L squared over twelve.
Rotation mirrors linear motion; translate the analogy table, do not memorise twice.
Rolling: v equals omega R; energy carries the bracket one plus K squared over R squared; the sphere wins the race.
Top exam traps: forgetting the j-term minus, mixing degrees and radians, and counting only translational energy.
Golden habit: check units, spell out the axis or reference point, and sanity-check every answer against intuition.

segments.text: And finally, the one-page cheat sheet, the ideas to carry into the exam hall.
Centre of mass: the whole body moves as if all its mass and all the external force were concentrated there, and no internal force can ever shift it.
Cross product: get the direction from the right-hand rule, compute it with the determinant, and never forget the minus sign on the j term.

Torque turns things, and the net torque equals the rate of change of angular momentum. When the external torque is zero, angular momentum is conserved; that one line solves skaters, collisions, and orbits.
Equilibrium needs both conditions together, the net force zero and the net torque zero, and the smart move is to take torques about an unknown force to make it vanish.
The must-know moments of inertia: a ring is M R squared, a disc is half M R squared, a solid sphere is two fifths M R squared, and a rod about its centre is M L squared over twelve.
All of rotational motion mirrors linear motion, so translate the analogy table rather than memorising a whole second set of formulas.
Rolling: the centre speed is omega R, the energy and speed carry the bracket one plus K squared over R squared, and the solid sphere always wins the race down a ramp.
Watch the top exam traps: the missing minus on the j term, mixing degrees with radians, and counting only the translational energy of a rolling body.

<excited> And the golden habit that spans the whole chapter: check your units, always name the axis or reference point, and sanity-check every answer against physical intuition. Do that, and this chapter becomes some of the most reliable marks on the paper.
और आख़िर में, one-page cheat sheet, वे ideas जो exam hall में ले जाने हैं।
Centre of mass — पूरी body ऐसे चलती है मानो उसकी सारी mass और सारा external force वहीं केंद्रित हों, और कोई internal force उसे कभी नहीं खिसका सकता।
Cross product — direction right-hand rule से लो, उसे determinant से compute करो, और j term पर minus sign कभी मत भूलो।
Torque चीज़ों को घुमाता है, और net torque बराबर angular momentum के change की rate। जब external torque zero हो, angular momentum conserved है; वही एक line skaters, collisions, और orbits हल करती है।
Equilibrium को दोनों conditions साथ चाहिए, net force zero और net torque zero, और चतुर चाल है torques किसी unknown force के बारे में लेना ताकि वह ग़ायब हो जाए।
Must-know moments of inertia — एक ring है M R square, एक disc आधा M R square, एक solid sphere two fifths M R square, और एक rod अपने centre के बारे में M L square बटा twelve।
पूरी rotational motion linear motion का mirror है, तो analogy table translate करो, formulas का पूरा दूसरा set रटने के बजाय।
Rolling — centre की speed है omega R, energy और speed bracket one plus K square बटा R square रखते हैं, और solid sphere ramp से नीचे race हमेशा जीतता है।
Top exam traps पर नज़र — j term पर छूटा minus, degrees को radians से मिलाना, और एक rolling body की सिर्फ़ translational energy गिनना।

<excited> और वह golden habit जो पूरे chapter में फैली है — अपने units check करो, हमेशा axis या reference point का नाम लो, और हर answer को physical intuition के सामने sanity-check करो। यह करो, और यह chapter paper के सबसे भरोसेमंद marks में से बन जाता है।
